text: This WEB SITE HOSTING AGREEMENT ("this Agreement") is entered into this 6th day of April, 1999 by and between Centrack International, a Florida corporation ("the Customer"), and i-on interactive, a Florida corporation ("i-on").

text: The term of this Agreement for the Hosted Site shall commence upon April 1, 1999 and shall continue for a period of six (6) months, unless earlier terminated in accordance with provisions hereof.

text:
This Agreement shall automatically be renewed for one (1) or more one (1) month periods unless either the Customer or i-on gives notice to the other party of its intention not to renew the

4 Agreement, which notice must be given not less than fifteen (15) days before the end of the respective initial or renewal term.

text: Either party may terminate this Agreement without cause at any time effective upon thirty (30) days' written notice.

text: i-on's liability for damages to the Customer for any cause whatsoever, regardless of the form of action, and whether in contract or in tort, including negligence, shall be limited to one (1) month's fees and the remaining portion of any prepaid fees.
rationale: Rule requires cap for both parties and 12 months' fees; clause limits only "i-on's liability" to "one (1) month's fees."

text: This Agreement was entered into in the State of Florida, and its validity, construction, interpretation, and legal effect shall be governed by the laws and judicial decisions of the State of Florida applicable to contracts entered into and performed entirely within the State of Florida.

text: This Co-Promotion Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into and dated as of September 26, 2018 (the "Effective Date") by and between Dova Pharmaceuticals, Inc., a Delaware corporation ("Dova"), and Valeant Pharmaceuticals North America LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("Valeant").
rationale: Rule: market practice. "entered into and dated as of September 26, 2018" is a standard agreement date with no one-sided obligation.

text: Dova and Valeant are each referred to individually as a "Party" and together as the "Parties".
rationale: Rule: market practice. "each referred to individually as a 'Party' and together as the 'Parties'" is standard, mutual definitional language.

text: "Effective Date" shall have the meaning set forth in the preamble to this Agreement.
rationale: Rule: market practice. "shall have the meaning set forth in the preamble" is a routine cross-reference creating no obligations.

text: 1.43 "Party" shall have the meaning set forth in the preamble to this Agreement.

During the Term, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, Dova hereby grants to Valeant the right, on a co-exclusive basis (solely with Dova and its Affiliates), to Detail and promote the Product in the Specialty in the Territory in the Field, and to conduct the Valeant Activities and the activities of the institutional account management team (pursuant to and subject to the terms of Section 4.1.5) for the Product in the Territory in the Field in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement.
rationale: Exclusivity rule requires business and legal approval; grant is "co-exclusive basis" and needs sign-off before execution.

text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Dova retains and reserves the right for Dova and its Affiliates to promote the Product in the Territory including in the Specialty.
rationale: Retains Dova's own promotion rights, which favors the company and needs no approval beyond the grant itself.

text: Except to Affiliates of Valeant, Valeant's rights and obligations under this Section 2.1 are non-transferable, non-assignable, and non-delegable.
rationale: Mutual-consent assignment rule is bypassed: "Except to Affiliates of Valeant" allows transfer without consent, a one-sided carve-out.

text: 2.2 Retention of Rights. Except with respect to the exclusive rights granted to Valeant to conduct the Valeant Activities for the Product in the Specialty in the Territory in the Field pursuant to Section 2.1 and, and if agreed upon, outside the Specialty in the Territory in the Field pursuant to Section 4.1.5, Dova retains all rights in and to the Product.
rationale: Retention of rights is favorable, but "and, and if agreed upon" is ambiguous on the scope of Valeant's rights outside the Specialty.

text: 2.3.1 Non-Competition. (a) [***], neither Valeant nor its Affiliates shall, directly or indirectly, [***] in the Territory other than the Product; provided that if the Agreement is terminated by Dova pursuant to [***], then any Tail Period shall be immediately terminated if either Valeant or any of its Affiliates, directly or indirectly, [***] in the Territory other than the Product during such Tail Period. Notwithstanding the foregoing, this Section 2.3.1(a) shall not apply to any products marketed, promoted, detailed, offered for sale, or sold by any business (or any portion thereof), other Person, or group of Persons, [***].
rationale: Restricts Valeant, not Dova; "neither Valeant nor its Affiliates shall" limits the counterparty's activity, which benefits the company.

text: (a) [***], neither Dova nor is Affiliates shall, directly or indirectly, [***]. Notwithstanding the foregoing, this Section 2.3.1(b) shall not apply to any products marketed, promoted, detailed, offered for sale, or sold by any business (or any portion thereof), other Person, or group of Persons[***].
rationale: Restricts Dova's own business; "neither Dova nor is Affiliates shall" triggers the rule that any restriction needs approval.

text: 2.3.2 Non-Solicitation. [***], neither Valeant nor Dova (nor any of their respective Affiliates) shall directly or indirectly solicit for hire or employee as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other Party's professional personnel who have had direct involvement with the JSC, with the Valeant Activities under this Agreement (which, in the case of Valeant, includes the Field Force Personnel) or with Dova's commercialization activities for the Product, without the other Party's prior written consent. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, in no event shall the restrictions set forth in this Section 2.3.2 apply to [***].
rationale: Mutual non-solicit ("neither Valeant nor Dova") is market-standard, though redacted carve-outs warrant a quick check.

text: For clarity, except as provided in Sections 2.1 or 2.4, Valeant shall not acquire any license or other intellectual property interest, by implication or otherwise, in any technology, Know-How or other intellectual property owned or controlled by Dova or any of its Affiliates, and Dova is not providing any such technology, Know-How or other intellectual property, or any assistance related thereto, to Valeant for any use other than for the mutual benefit of the Parties as expressly contemplated hereby.
rationale: Disclaims implied IP license to Valeant; "Valeant shall not acquire any license" protects Dova's technology.

text: 2.4.1 Valeant shall have the non-exclusive right to use the Dova Trademarks and Copyrights solely on Product Materials in order to perform the Valeant Activities and solely in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement.
rationale: Narrow, non-exclusive trademark license "solely on Product Materials" to Valeant; limited scope favors Dova.

text: Valeant shall have no rights under this Agreement in or to the Dova Trademarks and Copyrights except as specifically provided herein.
rationale: "Valeant shall have no rights... except as specifically provided herein" keeps Dova's marks reserved; favorable to company.

text: Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, [***]) and continuing throughout the remainder of the Term, Valeant shall maintain at least one hundred (100) Sales Representatives with responsibility to Detail the Product in the Specialty in the Territory.
rationale: Obligation falls on Valeant to maintain "at least one hundred (100) Sales Representatives"; a commitment benefiting Dova.

text: Except as set forth in this Agreement, without the prior written consent of Dova (not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned), Valeant shall not conduct any Valeant Activities, other than Detailing, with respect to the Product.
rationale: Rule: exclusive arrangements need business and legal approval. "shall not conduct any Valeant Activities" is exclusivity requiring that sign-off.

text: The Parties agree that these institutional account managers shall not be required to achieve any minimum number of Details.
rationale: Rule: flags deviations from market practice. "shall not be required to achieve any minimum number of Details" weakens Valeant's performance commitment.

text: As between the Parties, Dova shall own all right, title and interest in and to any Product Materials (and all content contained therein) and any Product Labeling (and all content contained therein), including applicable copyrights and trademarks (other than any name, trademark, trade name or logo of Valeant or its Affiliates that may appear on such Product materials or Product Labeling), and to the extent Valeant (or any of its Affiliates) obtains or otherwise has a claim to any of the foregoing, Valeant hereby assigns (and shall cause any applicable Affiliate to assign) all of its right, title and interest in and to such Product Materials (and content) and Product Labeling (and content) (other than any name, trademark, trade name or logo of Valeant or its Affiliates that may appear on such Product materials or Product Labeling) to Dova and Valeant agrees to (and shall cause its applicable Affiliate to) execute all documents and take all actions as are reasonably requested by Dova to vest title to such Product Materials (and content) and Product Labeling (and content) in Dova (or its designated Affiliate).
rationale: Playbook bars assigning company IP to counterparty; here Valeant assigns its rights to Dova: "Valeant hereby assigns... to Dova."

text: Valeant acknowledges and agrees that Dova will not maintain or procure any worker's compensation, healthcare, or other insurance for or on behalf of the Field Force Personnel, all of which shall be Valeant's sole responsibility.
rationale: Playbook flags one-sided terms: "all of which shall be Valeant's sole responsibility" shifts insurance burden entirely, a possible market deviation to verify.

text: Commencing with the Calendar Quarter commencing on October 1, 2018, as consideration for the Valeant Activities performed by Valeant, Dova shall pay Valeant a promotion fee based on annual Net Sales during the Term, calculated as follows:

text: In addition to the promotion fee above and as additional consideration for the performance of such Valeant Activities, Dova shall pay to Valeant a milestone payment in the amount of Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($2,500,000) when aggregate Net Sales in a Calendar Year first reach [***], payable within [***] after the end of the Calendar Quarter in which such Net Sales are reached.
rationale: Rule: flags one-sided or off-market terms. A fixed $2.5M payment triggered by Net Sales reaching a threshold is a common, performance-based milestone.

text: 7.1 Recordkeeping. Each Party shall maintain complete and accurate books and records in sufficient detail, in accordance with GAAP (to the extent applicable and in accordance with the Agreement) and all Applicable Law, to enable verification of the performance of such Party's obligations under this Agreement and any payments due to a Party under this Agreement. Unless otherwise specified herein, the books and records for a given Calendar Year of the Term shall be maintained for a period of [***] after the end of such Calendar Year or longer if required by Applicable Law.

7.2 Valeant Rights. Valeant shall have the right, at its own expense, during normal business hours and upon reasonable prior notice, through certified public accounting firm or other auditor selected by Valeant and reasonably acceptable to Dova and upon execution of a confidentiality agreement reasonably satisfactory to Dova in form and substance, to inspect and audit the applicable records and books maintained by Dova for purposes of verifying Dova's payment obligations within this Agreement, including the applicable records and books of account maintained by Dova, or any Affiliate, as applicable, with respect to Net Sales in order to confirm the accuracy and completeness of such records and books of account and all payments hereunder; provided, however, that (i) such examination shall not take place more often than once per every twelve (12) months during the Term and once during the one (1) year period following the end of the Term, and (ii) such examination shall not cover a period of time that has previously been audited; provided that Valeant shall have the right to conduct additional "for cause" audits to the extent necessary to address significant problems relating to Dova's payment obligations hereunder. Dova shall reasonably cooperate in any such inspection or audit conducted by Valeant. Any undisputed adjustments required as a result of overpayments or underpayments identified through the exercise of audit rights shall be made by payment to the Party owed such adjustment within [***] after identification of such adjustment. Valeant shall bear the out-of-pocket costs and expenses incurred by the Parties in connection with any such inspection or audit, unless the audit shows an undisputed under-reporting or underpayment for that audited period in excess of [***] of the amounts properly determined, in which case, Dova shall reimburse Valeant for its audit fees and reasonable out-of-pocket expenses in connection with said audit, which reimbursement shall be due and payable within [***] of receiving appropriate invoices and other support for such audit-related costs.
rationale: Audit rule: "Valeant shall bear..." cost-shifting to Dova above threshold and Valeant-only audit of Dova's payments is one-sided.

text: 7.3 Dova Rights. Dova shall have the right, at its own expense, during normal business hours and upon reasonable prior notice, through a certified public accounting firm or other auditor selected by Dova and reasonably acceptable to Valeant and upon execution of a confidentiality agreement reasonably satisfactory to Valeant in form and substance, to inspect and audit the applicable records and books maintained by Valeant relating to the Valeant Activities for purposes of verifying Valeant's compliance with the terms of this Agreement, provided that (i) such examination shall not take place more often than once per every twelve (12) months during the Term and once during the one (1) year period following the end of the Term, and (ii) such examination shall not cover a period of time that has previously been audited; provided that Dova shall have the right to conduct additional "for cause" audits to the extent necessary to address significant compliance problems relating to Valeant's obligations hereunder or in response to any inquiry, inspection, investigation or other requirements of a Government Authority in the Territory relating to the Valeant Activities. For purposes of clarity, any such inspection or audit described in this Section 7.3 shall be limited to only those books and records of Valeant that are applicable to Valeant's performance of its obligations under this Agreement. Where necessary, on reasonable request, Dova's audit rights shall include interviewing Sales Representatives and other employees of Valeant. Valeant shall reasonably cooperate in any such inspection or audit conducted by Dova. Any undisputed adjustments required as a result of overreporting the aggregate actual number of Details for the Product made by the Sales Representatives for a Calendar Quarter or the Quarterly Average Sales Force Size identified through the exercise of audit rights shall be made by payment by Valeant to Dova within [***] after identification of such adjustment.
rationale: Audit rule: Dova's audit is scope-limited ("limited to only those books and records") with Dova bearing its own costs; mostly balanced.

text: Dova shall bear the out-of-pocket costs and expenses incurred by the Parties in connection with any such inspection or audit, unless the audit shows an undisputed over- payment for that audited period in excess of [***] of the amounts properly determined, in which case, Valeant shall reimburse Dova for its audit fees and reasonable out-of-pocket expenses in connection with said audit, which reimbursement shall be due and payable within [***] of receiving appropriate invoices and other support for such audit-related costs.
rationale: Rule: flag deviations from market practice. Cost-shifting with a threshold and reimbursement is market-standard. Low risk.

text: [***], Valeant hereby grants to Dova a fully paid-up, royalty free, non-transferable, non- exclusive license (with a limited right to sub-license to its Affiliates) to any Valeant Property that appears on, embodied on or contained in the Product materials or Product Labeling solely for use in connection with Dova's promotion or other commercialization of the Product in the Territory.

text: Valeant agrees to assign, and hereby does assign, to Dova (and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their respective employees and other representatives to assign to Dova) any and all right, title and interest that Valeant (or any such Affiliates, employees or other representatives) may have in or to any Invention.

text: The ownership, and all goodwill from the use, of any Dova Trademarks and Copyrights shall at all times vest in and inure to the benefit of Dova, and Valeant shall assign, and hereby does assign, any rights it may have in the foregoing to Dova.

text: Dova represents and warrants to Valeant as of the Effective Date that:

it has the exclusive right to promote the Product in the Territory to the Target Professionals in the Specialty and the rights granted by it to Valeant hereunder do not conflict with any rights granted by Dova to any Third Party;

text: Valeant represents and warrants to Dova as of the Effective Date that:

NOTWITHSTANDING ANY OTHER PROVISION CONTAINED HEREIN (OTHER THAN AS SET FORTH IN THE SECOND SENTENCE OF THIS SECTION 11.4), IN NO EVENT SHALL DOVA (OR ITS AFFILIATES) OR VALEANT (OR ITS AFFILIATES) BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER OR ANY OF THE OTHER PARTY'S AFFILIATES FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES (INCLUDING LOST PROFITS) SUFFERED OR INCURRED BY SUCH OTHER PARTY OR ITS AFFILIATES THAT ARISE OUT OF OR RELATE TO THIS AGREEMENT OR IN CONNECTION WITH A BREACH OR ALLEGED BREACH OF THIS AGREEMENT, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, TORT, STRICT LIABILITY OR OTHERWISE, AND REGARDLESS OF ANY NOTICE OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.
rationale: Rule requires a cap of at least 12 months' fees; clause is mutual ("OR VALEANT") but excludes only consequential damages and sets no cap amount.

text: THE FOREGOING SENTENCE SHALL NOT LIMIT (1) THE OBLIGATIONS OF EITHER PARTY TO INDEMNIFY THE OTHER PARTY FROM AND AGAINST THIRD PARTY CLAIMS UNDER SECTION 11.1 OR 11.2, AS APPLICABLE, OR (2) DAMAGES AVAILABLE FOR A PARTY'S BREACH OF THE CONFIDENTIALITY AND NON-USE OBLIGATIONS IN ARTICLE 9.
rationale: Rule: "Uncapped liability needs legal approval." Carve-outs "SHALL NOT LIMIT" indemnity and confidentiality damages, leaving them uncapped.

text: 11.5 Insurance. Each Party acknowledges and agrees that during the Term, it shall maintain, through purchase or self- insurance, adequate insurance, including products liability coverage and comprehensive general liability insurance, adequate to cover its obligations under this Agreement and which are consistent with normal business practices of prudent companies similarly situated.
rationale: Mutual insurance duty, tied to 'consistent with normal business practices of prudent companies' — market standard.

text: Each Party shall provide reasonable written proof of the existence of such insurance to the other Party upon request.
rationale: Proof of insurance is mutual ('each Party') and on request, which is customary.

text: Dova does not and will not maintain or procure any worker's compensation, healthcare, or other insurance for or on behalf of any Field Force Personnel, all of which shall be Valeant's sole responsibility.
rationale: Flag one-sided obligations: 'all of which shall be Valeant's sole responsibility' places all Field Force insurance cost on one party.

text: For clarity, the insurance requirements of this Section 11.5 shall not be construed to create a limit of either Party's liability with respect to its indemnification obligations under this ARTICLE 11.
rationale: Insurance clause expressly does not cap indemnities, which is mutual and consistent with market practice.

text: 12.1 Term. This Agreement shall become effective as of the Effective Date and, unless earlier terminated as provided in this ARTICLE 12, shall extend until the four (4) year anniversary of the Effective Date (the "Term").
rationale: Flag deviations from market: a fixed 'four (4) year' term with no renewal mechanism is long and locks in obligations.

text: 12.3.1 Either Party shall have the right to terminate this Agreement before the end of the Term for its convenience upon [***] written notice to the other Party (and any such termination shall become effective at the end of such [***]); [***].

text: 12.5 Tail Period. Solely in the event that Dova has terminated this Agreement pursuant to Section 12.3.1 and notwithstanding anything else herein, in consideration of the promotion services performed by Valeant during the Term, with respect to the Tail Period, Dova shall make payments to Valeant in an amount equal to [***] of the amounts that would have been payable by Dova to Valeant with respect to such Tail Period pursuant to Section 6.1 had the Agreement not been so terminated.
rationale: Flag one-sided obligations: Dova pays tail amounts only 'solely in the event that Dova has terminated' for convenience.

text: 13.2 Assignment. Except as provided in this Section 13.2, this Agreement may not be assigned or otherwise transferred, nor may any rights or obligations hereunder be assigned or transferred, by either Party, without the written consent of the other Party (such consent not to be unreasonably withheld); provided that a merger, sale of stock or comparable transaction shall not constitute an assignment.
rationale: Assignment rule requires both parties' consent, but 'not to be unreasonably withheld' and the merger carve-out weaken it.

text: Any attempted assignment not in accordance with this Section 13.2 shall be void.
rationale: Standard provision voiding non-compliant assignments; consistent with the prior written consent requirement.

cid: PACIRA PHARMACEUTICALS, INC. - A_R STRATEGIC LICENSING, DISTRIBUTION AND MARKETING AGREEMENT
text: 20.1 Assignment. Subject to Section 20.2, neither Party shall, nor shall it purport to, assign, license, transfer or change any of its rights or  obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld  conditioned or delayed; provided, however, that except as provided in Section 20.4 either Party may assign its rights hereunder to an  Affiliate or to any successor by merger, consolidation, sale of stock or other equity interests or the sale of substantially all of the assets of  such Party without the consent of the other Party.
rationale: Anti-Assignment rule requires consent of both parties, but the 'provided, however' proviso allows assignment to Affiliates or merger successors 'without the consent of the other Party.'

cid: PACIRA PHARMACEUTICALS, INC. - A_R STRATEGIC LICENSING, DISTRIBUTION AND MARKETING AGREEMENT
text: 20.4 Change of Control. cid: PACIRA PHARMACEUTICALS, INC. - A_R STRATEGIC LICENSING, DISTRIBUTION AND MARKETING AGREEMENT

text: This INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AGREEMENT (this "Agreement" or "IPA"), effective as of this 30  day of June 2016 (the "Effective Date") among THE HERTZ CORPORATION, a Delaware corporation, with an address of 8501 Williams Road, Estero, Florida 33928 (hereinafter "THC"); HERTZ SYSTEM, INC., a Delaware corporation, with an address of 8501 Williams Road, Estero, Florida 33928, United States of America (hereinafter "HSI") and HERC RENTALS INC., a Delaware corporation, with an address of 27500 Riverview Center Blvd., Bonita Springs, Florida 34134, United States of America (hereinafter "HERC") (hereinafter referred to collectively as the "Parties" and individually as a "Party").
rationale: Party identification only; no rule-relevant obligation. Addresses and entity names are routine.

text: "Interim Period" means a period of four (4) years commencing from the Effective Date of this Agreement.
rationale: Playbook flags market deviations: "a period of four (4) years" is a long interim term for a transitional license.

text: HSI will retain ownership of the worldwide rights in and to the VRB Trademarks.

text: HSI will retain ownership and will grant a royalty-free, non-exclusive license to HERC to use the HSI (HERTZ) Foreign ERB Trademarks (those foreign trademarks owned by HSI related to the ERB that incorporate the mark/name HERTZ) as set forth on Schedule A, for the Interim Period, outside the United States and Puerto Rico, as more fully set forth in the Trademark, Trade Name, Domain and Related Rights License Agreement attached as Exhibit A.
rationale: Playbook flags one-sided grants: "royalty-free, non-exclusive license" of HERTZ foreign marks, time-limited but without royalty.

text: HSI will retain ownership and will grant a royalty-free, non-exclusive, license to HERC to use the HSI (HERTZ) US ERB Trademarks (those US trademarks   3  owned by HSI related to the ERB that incorporate the mark/name HERTZ) as set forth on Schedule B, for the Interim Period, in the United States and Puerto Rico, as more fully set forth in the Trademark, Trade Name, Domain and Related Rights License Agreement attached as Exhibit A.
rationale: Playbook flags one-sided grants: "royalty-free, non-exclusive" license of HERTZ US marks in the United States and Puerto Rico.

text: HSI will assign all right, title and interest in and to the HSI HERC Foreign ERB Trademarks (those foreign trademarks owned by HSI related to the ERB for the HERC trademarks) as set forth on Schedule C to HERC as more fully set forth in the Trademark Assignment Agreements attached hereto as Exhibit B-1 (Canada) and Exhibit B-2 (all other foreign countries).
rationale: Ip Ownership rule violated: "HSI will assign all right, title and interest" in HERC foreign ERB trademarks to HERC.

text: HERC will have the right to retain ownership and use of the HERC (HERTZ) US ERB Trademarks (those US trademarks owned by HERC related to the ERB that incorporate the mark/name HERTZ) as set forth on Schedule D for the Interim Period.
rationale: Ip Ownership rule: HERC retains HERTZ-incorporating US marks, "retain ownership and use", diluting company brand control.

text: HERC shall retain ownership and the right to use the HERC (HERC) US ERB Trademarks (those US trademarks owned by HERC related to the ERB that do not incorporate the mark/name HERTZ) as set forth on Schedule E.
rationale: Ip Ownership rule: "HERC shall retain ownership" of marks not incorporating HERTZ; company IP not affected.

text: HERC shall retain ownership and the right to use the HERC (HERC) Foreign ERB Trademarks (those foreign trademarks owned by HERC related to the ERB that do not incorporate the mark/name HERTZ) as set forth on Schedule F.
rationale: Ip Ownership rule: "HERC shall retain ownership" of foreign marks without HERTZ; no company IP transferred.

text: THC will retain ownership and will, subject to compliance with the terms of this Agreement, grant a royalty-free, non-exclusive license to HERC to use the THC (HERTZ) ERB Domains (those domains owned by THC related to the ERB that   4  incorporate the mark/name HERTZ) as set forth on Schedule G, for the Interim Period, as more fully set forth in the Trademark, Trade Name, Domain and Related Rights License Agreement.
rationale: License Grant: THC retains domains and grants a license "subject to compliance" for the Interim Period; conditional and time-limited.

text: THC will assign all right, title and interest in and to the THC ERB Domains (those domains owned by THC related to the ERB that do not incorporate the mark/name HERTZ) as set forth on Schedule H to HERC and as more fully set forth in the Domain Name Assignment attached hereto as Exhibit D.
rationale: Ip Ownership rule violated: "THC will assign all right, title and interest" in ERB Domains to HERC.

text: HSI will, subject to compliance with the terms of this Agreement, grant a royalty-free, non-exclusive worldwide license to HERC to use the mark/name HERTZ as part of company names for the Interim Period, as more fully set forth in the Trademark, Trade Name, Domain and Related Rights License Agreement attached as Exhibit A.
rationale: Playbook flags one-sided grants: "royalty-free, non-exclusive worldwide license" to use HERTZ in company names.

text: THC and/or HSI will retain ownership and will grant a royalty-free, non-exclusive license to HERC to use such Other Intellectual Property for the Interim Period, as more fully set forth in the Trademark, Trade Name, Domain and Related Rights License Agreement attached as Exhibit A.
rationale: Playbook flags one-sided grants: "royalty-free, non-exclusive license" of undefined "Other Intellectual Property" with unclear scope.

text: Nothing in this Agreement or the other ancillary agreements thereto shall affect or limit the rights confirmed in the license effective April 1, 1998 between HSI and HERC, and the sublicense effective April 1, 1998 between HERC as Sub-Licensor and Matthews Equipment Limited and Hertz Canada Equipment Rental Partnership as Sub-Licensees, which remain in full force and effect, save and except that such license and sublicense shall not expire before the later of the expiration of the Interim Period or the final determination or resolution of the action pending as T- 409-16 in the Federal Court of Canada (including any appeals thereof).
rationale: Playbook flags one-sided terms: license "shall not expire before the later of" the Interim Period or the Canadian litigation's resolution.

text: During the Interim Period, neither HERC nor any of its affiliates or subsidiaries shall, directly or indirectly, engage in the business of renting or leasing cars, crossovers or light trucks (including sport utility vehicles and light commercial vehicles) in [any country in which THC or any of its affiliates or subsidiaries rents or leases cars, crossovers or light trucks (including sport utility vehicles and light commercial vehicles) as of the date of this Agreement] without THC's prior written consent, except to the extent materially consistent in type and scope with HERC's operations immediately prior to the date of this IPA.
rationale: Restriction on company business: 'shall... engage in the business of renting or leasing cars' during Interim Period, needing THC consent. Playbook requires approval for any restriction.

text: This Agreement and all disputes or controversies arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the transactions contemplated hereby shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the internal laws of the State of New York, without regard to the laws of any other jurisdiction that might be applied because of the conflicts of laws principles of the State of New York.
rationale: Mutual New York governing law with standard conflicts language is market practice; no one-sided obligation flagged.

text: HERC may not assign, transfer, sublicense or delegate any of its rights hereunder or delegate its obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of HSI, and any such purported assignment, transfer, sublicense or delegation, in the absence of such consent, shall be void and without effect.
rationale: 'HERC may not assign... without the prior written consent of HSI' binds only HERC, not both parties as the playbook requires.

text: This Agreement shall be binding upon and shall inure to the benefit of all successors and assigns of the Parties (including by way of merger or sale of all or substantially all assets), subject to the restrictions on assignment set forth herein.
rationale: Binding on successors and assigns is standard, and 'subject to the restrictions on assignment set forth herein' preserves consent requirements.

text: The amount of coverage shall be a minimum of three million dollars ($3,000,000) combined single limit, with no deductible amount for each single occurrence for bodily injury and/or property damage.
rationale: 'Minimum of three million dollars' with no deductible is a conventional coverage term and not a one-sided burden.

text: HERC shall provide for ten (10) days notice to THC and HSI in the event of any modification, cancellation or termination.
rationale: Playbook flags one-sided obligations: only 'HERC shall provide for ten (10) days notice' of cancellation, with no reciprocal duty and a short notice period.

text: HERC agrees to furnish THC and HSI Certificates of Insurance evidencing same within thirty (30) days after the execution of this Agreement.
rationale: Delivering certificates 'within thirty (30) days after the execution' is a routine administrative obligation and not one-sided in substance.

text: Except as otherwise provided hereunder in Section 5.2 and Section 5.3 with respect to indemnified parties, nothing contained in this Agreement shall be construed to create any third-party beneficiary rights in any individual.
rationale: Disclaiming third-party beneficiary rights except indemnified parties is market-standard and carves out only expected exceptions.

text: COOPERATION AGREEMENT
rationale: Document title only; no obligations. Consistent with the playbook's market-practice rule.

text: This Cooperation Agreement (2014 Amendment) (this "Agreement") is entered into on January 24, 2014 in Beijing by and between:
rationale: Standard dating recital; no deviation from market practice flagged.

text: (1) Nanjing Tuniu Technology Co., Ltd., with its registered address at 3-5/F Building No.6, Southeast University Science Park, 6 Changjianghou Street, Xuanwu District, Nanjing and its legal representative being Yu Dunde ("Party A");
rationale: Standard party identification; no one-sided obligation created.

text: (2) Beijing Tuniu Technology Co., Ltd., with its registered address at R1006 10/F Building No.4, Yard No.1 of Shangdishi Street, Haidian District, Beijing and its legal representative being Yu Dunde ("Party B").
rationale: Standard party identification; no one-sided obligation created.

text: This Agreement shall take effect as of the date when the authorized representatives of the Parties sign hereon.
rationale: Effective on signature by authorized representatives; standard mechanics.

text: Party A and Party B agree and confirm that the term of cooperation under this Agreement shall commence from the execution date hereof and end on the expiration date of the operation term of Party B ("Term of Cooperation").
rationale: Playbook market-practice rule: term tied to "expiration date of the operation term of Party B", an external, open-ended end date.

text: Party A irrevocably undertakes that Party A will take Party B as its exclusive and sole partner to provide the business consultancy and technical services as well as technical consultancy to Party A and its subsidiaries. Party A shall not establish any same or similar cooperative relationship with any third party in respect of such businesses nor shall it make any same or similar arrangement, unless with the prior written consent of Party B.
rationale: Exclusivity rule needs approval: "exclusive and sole partner" binds only Party A, blocking third-party arrangements.

text: Party A irrevocably undertakes that it will make best efforts to assist and endeavor to achieve the exclusive operation of thecooperative business to the extent permitted by laws.
rationale: Exclusivity rule: "best efforts to assist and endeavor to achieve the exclusive operation" imposes open-ended effort obligations on Party A.

text: Party A irrevocably undertakes that, without Party B's consent, Party A shall not conduct any other business or make any commercial arrangement, including without limitation being engaged in or otherwise participating in any commercial activities and businesses independently or together with any other person or entity, nor shall it carry out any activities that may be competitive with or cause adverse effect to Party B's business.
rationale: Business restriction rule needs approval: "shall not conduct any other business" is a broad non-compete on Party A.

text: Party B shall have the right to terminate this Agreement in advance without the prior written consent from Party A, bysending a written notice to Party A but Party A may not terminate or rescind this Agreement;
rationale: Termination rule (90-day notice): Party B may terminate by notice while "Party A may not terminate", with no notice period.

text: Party A and Party B unanimously agree that they will allocate the proceeds generated from cooperation in accordance with thefollowing provisions:
rationale: Allocation framing is mutual ("unanimously agree"); substance depends on provisions not shown.

text: The total sum of Service Fee shall be equal to the amount of profits gained by Party A or its subsidiaries who have accepted Party B's Services.
rationale: One-sided rule: Service Fee equals "the amount of profits gained by Party A", an unusual uncapped profit share.

text: Except as otherwise agreed hereunder, if Party A or its subsidiaries fail to pay the Service Fee in full on schedule according to provisions of Article 4.1 and Article 4.2, then Party A or its subsidiaries shall, in addition to the continuance of the payment of Service Fee in full, it shall pay Party B the liquidated damages at a daily interest rate of 0.03% in respect of the outstanding Service Fee.
rationale: Pre-set damages rule needs legal approval: "daily interest rate of 0.03%" plus continued fee payment acts as a penalty.

text: The demand for liquidated damages and specific performance in respect of any breach during the Term of Cooperation are all remedies that the non-breaching Party shall have under this Agreement.
rationale: Remedies rule: liquidated damages and specific performance are "all remedies", limiting other recourse; needs legal review.

text: The rights and obligations of each Party under this Agreement shall not be transferred, except for the transfer by Party B to its affiliates.
rationale: Assignment rule requires both parties' written consent; only Party B may transfer "to its affiliates".

text: The Parties agree that any and all intellectual property researched and developed, created and invented by the Parties (including their employees) in the course of performance of this Agreement shall be owned by Party B.
rationale: IP rule: jointly developed IP "shall be owned by Party B", assigning company IP to the counterparty.

text: This Agreement shall be governed by and interpreted pursuant to the laws of the People's Republic of China that are promulgated and are publicly available, provided that the general international business practices shall apply if the laws of the People's Republic of China that are promulgated and are publicly available do not involve any matter in relation to this Agreement.
rationale: PRC governing law is a standard choice; the international-practice fallback is minor.

text: Party A: Nanjing Tuniu Technology Co., Ltd.
rationale: Playbook rule: flag one-sided obligations. Clause only identifies "Party A: Nanjing Tuniu Technology Co., Ltd."; no obligations imposed.

text: Party B: Beijing Tuniu Technology Co., Ltd.
rationale: Playbook rule: flag one-sided obligations. Clause only identifies "Party B: Beijing Tuniu Technology Co., Ltd."; no obligations imposed.

text: PROMOTION AGREEMENT
rationale: Document title only; no obligations or deviation from market practice.

text: This Promotion Agreement (the "Agreement") is dated as of January 26, 1998 between CNET, Inc. ("CNET") and Cyberian Outpost, Inc. (the "Company").
rationale: Dating and party identification only; no one-sided obligations.

text: The term of this Agreement (the "Term") will begin on February 1, 1998 and end on the first anniversary of the date of this Agreement; provided that (a) either party may terminate this Agreement, effective at any time after the first three months of the Term, by giving 30 days' written notice of termination to the other party, and (b) either party may terminate this Agreement at any time by giving written notice of termination to the other party, if the other party commits a material breach of its obligations hereunder that is not cured within 30 days after notice thereof from the non-breaching party.
rationale: Rule requires at least 90 days' notice, but clause allows termination "by giving 30 days' written notice."

text: Subject to Section 4 below, CNET will provide the Company with a total of at least (a) [XXXXXX] Retail Impressions during the first three months of the Term, (b) [XXXXXX] Retail Impressions during the second three months of the Term, (c) [XXXXXX] Retail Impressions during the third three months of the Term, and (d) [XXXXXX] Retail Impressions during the fourth three months of the Term.
rationale: Obligation falls on CNET to deliver impressions, which benefits the Company.

text: If CNET fails to provide the Retail Impressions required by the preceding sentence during the Term, then CNET will continue to display Retail Impressions in accordance with this Agreement following the Term (notwithstanding the termination or expiration of the Term) until the required number of Retail Impressions has been delivered.
rationale: Obligation falls on CNET to keep delivering impressions post-term, favoring the Company.

text: For the purposes of clarity, the "fold" is defined as the visible portion of the screen on a standard 640 x 480 screen size.
For each month during the Term, the Company will pay CNET a minimum of [XXXX] in cash, plus [XXX] of CNET Sales.
rationale: "will pay CNET a minimum of" creates a fixed monthly payment obligation on the Company regardless of performance.

text: Exclusivity. For purposes of this agreement "Competing Computer Products Retailer" means any company other than the Company that is engaged in the retail sale of computer products, with the exception of CNET Direct, which operates BuyDirect.com. During the Term, CNET will not enter into more than two other agreements under which CNET receives consideration from a Competing Computer Products Retailer for displaying permanent links to or other fixed promotions for such Competing Computer Products Retailer on any CNET Site;
rationale: Restricts CNET to "not more than two other agreements" with competitors; exclusive-type terms need business and legal approval.

text: provided that the foregoing will not restrict the display of(a) standard advertisements for any Competing Computer Products Retailer or its products or (b) any promotions within COMPUTERS.COM or within CNET's Snap! Online service (which are expressly excluded from this provision).
rationale: Carve-outs for "standard advertisements" and COMPUTERS.COM promotions weaken the Company's exclusivity protection.

text: The parties acknowledge that the foregoing will not prevent CNET from displaying text links and other references to Competing Computer Products Retailers as reasonably necessary to provide appropriate editorial and search related services on the CNET Sites.
rationale: "will not prevent CNET from displaying text links" to competitors broadly erodes the exclusivity protection.

text: The Retail Promotions granted to the Company shall be placed in such a way as to provide no more or less prominence to the Company than is provided to any other Competing Computer Retailer signing an agreement with CNET.
rationale: Most-favored-nation prominence protection benefits the Company; the obligation sits on CNET.

text: The Company hereby grants to CNET a non-exclusive, royalty-free license, effective throughout the Term, to use, display and publish any of the Company trademarks, tradenames, service marks and logos that may be delivered by the Company to CNET expressly for inclusion in the Promotions, solely for use in connection with the Promotions.
rationale: License is limited to "solely for use in connection with the Promotions" and the Term, so scope is narrow.

text: CNET acknowledges and agrees that, as between the Company and CNET, the Company is the sole owner of all rights in and to the Company Marks.
rationale: CNET acknowledges "the Company is the sole owner" of Company Marks, which protects Company IP.

text: Each party will have the right to engage an independent third party to audit the books and records of the other party relevant to the calculation of Retail Impressions or CNET Sales, upon reasonable notice and during normal business hours, and the other party will provide reasonable cooperation in connection with any such audit. The party requesting the audit will pay all expenses of the auditor unless the audit reveals an underpayment by the other party of more than 5%, in which case the other party will reimburse all reasonable expenses of the auditor.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. "Each party will have the right" makes audit rights mutual, with market-standard 5% cost-shifting.

text: This Agreement will be construed in accordance with and governed by the laws of the State of California, without regard to principles of  conflicts of law.
rationale: Rule: flag market deviations. "governed by the laws of the State of California" is a neutral, standard governing-law choice.

text: This Agreement may not be assigned by either party, except (a) to the transferee of substantially all of the business operations of such party (whether by asset sale, stock sale, merger or otherwise) or (b) to any entity that controls, is controlled by or is under common control with such party.
rationale: Rule: assignment requires prior written consent of both parties. "may be assigned... except" permits assignment without consent.

text: CNET, INC.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. "CNET, INC." is only a party name with no obligations attached.

text: Cyberian Outpost
rationale: Rule: flag market deviations. "Cyberian Outpost" lacks an entity type or legal designation, creating ambiguity about the contracting party.

text: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AGREEMENT
rationale: Playbook rule on market deviation: 'INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AGREEMENT' is a neutral document title with no obligations.

text: This Intellectual Property Agreement (the "Agreement"), is entered into as of November 20, 2007 (the "Effective Date"), by and between Morgan Stanley & Co. Incorporated, a Delaware corporation ("MS") and MSCI Inc., a Delaware corporation ("MSCI").
rationale: Playbook rule on market deviation: a standard effective date and party identification with no one-sided terms.

text: (MS and MSCI individually referred to as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties").
rationale: Playbook rule on market deviation: a standard defined-terms convention for 'Party' and 'Parties' with no obligations.

text: "Trigger Date" means the date upon which Morgan Stanley shall cease to own more than 50% of the issued and outstanding shares of MSCI common stock.
rationale: Playbook rule on change of control: 'Trigger Date' keyed to MS ceasing to own 50%; confirm it gives no termination or renegotiation right.

text: MS hereby grants (subject to any existing third party contractual obligations) to MSCI a non-exclusive, perpetual, irrevocable, world- wide, royalty-free license for MSCI to use, modify, copy, create derivative works of and sublicense, for any business purpose, the MS Licensed Materials.

text: MSCI hereby grants (subject to any existing third party contractual obligations) to MS a non-exclusive, perpetual, irrevocable, world- wide, royalty-free license for MS to use, modify, copy, create derivative works of and sublicense, for any business purpose, the MSCI Licensed Materials.
rationale: Playbook rule on perpetual licenses: 'perpetual, irrevocable... royalty-free' grant to MS is broad but reciprocal, reducing one-sidedness.

text: This Agreement shall be construed in accordance with and governed by the substantive internal laws of the State of New York.
rationale: Playbook rule on governing law: 'substantive internal laws of the State of New York' is a common, neutral choice.

text: Any action seeking to enforce any provision of, or based on any matter arising out of or in connection with, this Agreement or the transactions contemplated hereby shall be brought in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York or any other New York State court sitting in New York County, and each of the parties hereby consents to the jurisdiction of such courts (and of the appropriate appellate courts therefrom) in any such suit, action or proceeding and irrevocably waives, to the fullest extent permitted by law, any objection which it may now or hereafter have to the laying of the venue of any such suit, action or proceeding in any such court or that any such suit, action or proceeding which is brought in any such court has been brought in an inconvenient forum.
rationale: Playbook rule on governing law: mutual 'consents to the jurisdiction' and venue waiver are standard for New York forum clauses.

text: This Agreement is not intended to confer upon any person or entity other than the parties hereto any rights or remedies hereunder.
rationale: Playbook rule on third-party beneficiaries: 'not intended to confer upon any person... other than the parties' is market standard.

text: Strategic Alliance Agreement
rationale: Rule flags market-deviating or one-sided terms; the title "Strategic Alliance Agreement" creates no obligations.

text: AGREEMENT made as of  , 2013, between Freedom Mortgage Corporation, a New Jersey corporation ("Freedom Mortgage"), and Cherry Hill Mortgage Investment Corp., a Maryland corporation ("Cherry Hill").

text: FREEDOM MORTGAGE CORPORATION
rationale: Playbook rule: deviation or one-sided obligations. "FREEDOM MORTGAGE CORPORATION" is a party name only, with no obligations imposed.

text: CHERRY HILL MORTGAGE INVESTMENT CORP.
rationale: Playbook rule: deviation or one-sided obligations. "CHERRY HILL MORTGAGE INVESTMENT CORP." is a party name only, with no obligations imposed.

text: IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties hereto have executed this Agreement as of the date first above-written.

Unless earlier terminated as provided below, this Agreement shall remain in effect until the later to occur of the date that is (x) three (3) years from the date hereof and (y) the date on which an affiliate of Freedom Mortgage is not acting as the external manager of Cherry Hill.
rationale: Playbook rule: deviation or one-sided obligations. "the date on which an affiliate of Freedom Mortgage is not acting" makes duration open-ended and tied to a third party's role.

text: This Agreement shall be binding upon and shall inure to the benefit of the Parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns; provided, however, that neither this Agreement nor any of the rights, interests or obligations hereunder shall be assigned by any Party without the prior written consent of the other Party.
rationale: Playbook rule: assignment needs both parties' consent. "without the prior written consent of the other Party" matches the rule and is mutual.

text: Nothing in this Agreement is intended to confer upon any other Person any rights or remedies under or by reason of this Agreement.
rationale: Playbook rule: deviation or one-sided obligations. "Nothing in this Agreement is intended to confer" disclaims third-party rights, which is standard and mutual.

text: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York, without giving effect to its principles of conflicts of laws, other than Section 5-1401 of the New York General Obligations Law.
rationale: Playbook rule: deviation or one-sided obligations. "governed by the laws of the State of New York" is a conventional, neutral choice of law.

text: Each Party agrees that during the Term of this Agreement and for a period of six (6) months thereafter it shall not, without the prior written  consent of the other Party, either on its own account or through its employees or agents or otherwise or on behalf of any other person,  firm, company or other organisation and other than by general advertising, solicit, interfere with, procure or entice away (or, in each case,  attempt so to do), either directly or indirectly, any employee or contractor of the other Party.
rationale: Playbook: flag one-sided obligations. Mutual "Each Party agrees" no-solicit with general advertising carve-out is market standard.

text: W2E agrees not to engage in business dealings, discussions, or otherwise work directly with any third parties introduced to W2E  through SHBV, or to exploit any pre-existing relationship of SHBV with any third party that has been represented to W2E by SHBV,  without the prior consent and/or direct participation of SHBV.
rationale: Playbook: exclusive arrangements need approval; one-sided. Only "W2E agrees not to engage" while SHBV keeps its rights.

text: SHBV agrees not to engage in business dealings, discussions, or otherwise work directly with any third parties introduced to SHBV  through W2E, or to exploit any pre-existing relationship of W2E with any third party that has been represented to SHBV by W2E,  without the prior consent and/or direct participation of W2E.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "SHBV agrees not to" binds only SHBV; the mirror clause is one-directional against that party.

text: Except as expressly agreed otherwise in writing, all Intellectual Property Rights vested in a Party prior to the date of this Agreement shall  remain vested in that Party. Further, any improvements, enhancements, modifications or developments to a Party's intellectual property  shall automatically vest in that Party irrespective of who generates the relevant improvement, enhancement, modification or development.
rationale: Rule: no IP assignment. "shall remain vested in that Party" and improvements "automatically vest in that Party," so nothing is assigned away.

text: Each Party grants to the other Party a non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free licence to use the other Party's Intellectual Property Rights  as far is strictly necessary to comply with its marketing and promotional obligations under this Agreement. For the sake of certainty, the  licence created by this Agreement does not extend to the use of the other Party's Intellectual Property Rights for any other commercial  purpose.
rationale: Rule: one-sided terms. The license is mutual, "non-exclusive," "non-transferable," and limited to "strictly necessary" marketing use.

text: The licence granted in Clause 10.2 above will automatically expire at the end of the Term of this Agreement.
The parties may terminate this Agreement at any time by mutual consent.
rationale: Rule: 90-day notice for counterparty convenience termination. "By mutual consent" gives no unilateral exit, so the rule is not triggered.

text: Each party may terminate this Agreement without liability if, despite their best efforts, the parties fail to conclude the Manufacturing  Agreement pursuant to Clauses 10 - 13 of this Agreement within one month from the date of this Agreement.
This Agreement shall come into force on the date given at the beginning of this Agreement.
rationale: Rule: market practice. "come into force on the date given" is a standard, mutual effective-date term.

text: This Agreement shall not take  effect until it has been executed by both the Parties.
rationale: Rule: market practice. "not take effect until it has been executed by both the Parties" is mutual and standard.

text: A person who is not a party to this Agreement may not enforce any of its provisions under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act  1999.
rationale: Rule: market practice. "may not enforce any of its provisions" under the 1999 Act is a standard exclusion.

text: This Agreement is governed by English law.
rationale: Rule: market practice. "governed by English law" is a neutral, commonly used governing law clause.

text: The Parties submit to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.
rationale: Rule: market practice. "non-exclusive jurisdiction" is mutual and gives both parties flexibility to sue elsewhere.

("Association"), an Ohio not-for profit corporation, with its principal place of business located at 2451 Crystal Drive, Suite 900, Arlington, VA 22202.
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: standard party identification with no deviating obligations.

text: ADA and/or Company may be referred to as a "Party" or collectively as the "Parties."
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: standard defined-term language, mutual and neutral.

text: This Agreement shall commence on March 15, 2018 and will expire on March 14, 2020 unless terminated earlier pursuant to Section 13 of the Agreement (the "Term").
rationale: Flag deviating terms: fixed two-year term, standard and mutual, with no unusual obligations.

text: (ii) ten (10) business days written notice to the other Party whenever the notifying Party in its sole discretion determines that the continuation of the Agreement will damage its reputation or good will;
rationale: Rule requires 90 days notice; clause allows "ten (10) business days written notice" in "sole discretion."

text: (e) is subject to a change of control (whether by merger, stock transfer or otherwise), except in the case of an initial public offering.
rationale: Rule requires approval for change-of-control termination; clause says "is subject to a change of control" with IPO carve-out.

text: 18. Non-Assignment: This Agreement shall be between the Parties only, and does not grant rights to any other party. This Agreement may not be assigned by either Party without the prior written consent of the other Party.
rationale: Rule requires mutual consent; "without the prior written consent of the other Party" matches it.

text: However, Company may only assign its responsibilities under this Agreement with Association's prior written approval as provided in Section 18.
rationale: Rule requires mutual consent; "prior written approval" from Association is consistent, though one-directional.

text: This Agreement shall be binding on the parties, and on their successors and assigns, without regard to whether it is expressly acknowledged in any instrument of succession or assignment.
rationale: Assignment rule: binding on "successors and assigns" is standard and mutual; no added exposure.

text: The Association is the sole and exclusive owner of its name and logos, with or without accompanying words, and has the legal right to enter into this Agreement.
rationale: IP rule: Association owns "its name and logos"; no Company IP transferred.

text: Company is the sole and exclusive owner of its name, logos, and marks (the "Company Marks"), which include, without limitation, the names, logos, and marks listed in Attachment B as Company Marks.
rationale: IP rule: "Company is the sole and exclusive owner" of Company Marks; Company retains its IP.

text: Company shall be the sole and exclusive owner of all materials created by or for the Company hereunder, with the exception of the Association Marks.
rationale: IP rule: "Company shall be the sole and exclusive owner of all materials" retains Company ownership.

text: The Association grants Company a non-exclusive, limited, revocable and conditional license during the term to use the Association Marks, solely to identify Company as a supporter of the Association.
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: Company's license is "revocable and conditional" and limited to the term.

text: The Company grants the Association a non-exclusive, limited, revocable and conditional license during the term to use the Company Marks, solely to identify Company as a supporter of the Association.
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: reciprocal license to Association mirrors Company's license terms.

text: Company may not permit any third party to use the Association Marks without the express prior written approval of the Association, which may be withheld for any reason.
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: approval "may be withheld for any reason" gives Association unilateral control.

text: During the term of this Agreement, and before any sponsorship or promotional activities are conducted under this Agreement, Company shall obtain and maintain at its expense, Commercial General Liability Insurance coverage with an insurance carrier with a Best's rating of A+.
rationale: Flag deviating terms: "Best's rating of A+" carrier requirement is stringent and adds cost.

text: The insurance shall be in an amount of: $2,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate with a $2,000,000 aggregate for products and completed operations.
rationale: Flag deviating terms: "$2,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate" plus products coverage exceeds typical sponsorship limits.

text: The Association must be a named additional insured, and shall be provided at least 30 days' notice for cancellation of policy and 10 days' notice for non-payment of premium.
rationale: Flag one-sided terms: Association as "named additional insured" with extended notice rights favors counterparty.

text: Such insurance shall be primary and non-contributory.
rationale: Flag deviating terms: "primary and non-contributory" shifts coverage burden to Company's policy.

text: Governing Law: This Agreement is subject to and shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the Commonwealth of Virginia with jurisdiction and venue in federal and Virginia courts in Alexandria and Arlington, Virginia.
rationale: Governing law: "Commonwealth of Virginia" and venue in Alexandria/Arlington courts are conventional and not one-sided.

text: The Association hereby grants Company the right to use the Association Name and Logo ("the Association Marks") on educational, promotional and or advertising materials throughout the Term (see Attachment "B").
rationale: License grant: "hereby grants Company the right to use" the Association Marks benefits the company; main gap is no approval terms.

text: For the purposes of this Agreement, funds raised through the pin pad/POS donation campaign shall be applied towards Company's total sponsorship of $150,000 for the Term.
rationale: Minimum commitment: campaign funds "shall be applied towards" the $150,000 total is ambiguous and could raise the company's payment obligation.

text: Company agrees to pay to the Association the cash rights fee in the amount of $150,000 for this Sponsorship Agreement.
rationale: Minimum commitment: "agrees to pay... $150,000" is an unconditional fee with no performance terms, and overlaps item 2.

text: co-venture arrangement (% of every purchase of in store apps goes to Association)

text: Signatures: American Diabetes Association Freeze Tag, Inc.
rationale: Parties: signature block "American Diabetes Association Freeze Tag, Inc." blurs the contracting entities and creates enforceability uncertainty.

text: This Agreement (including its Exhibit A and all other documents referenced herein) is entered into by eGain Communications Corporation ("eGain") and Eliance Corporation ("Customer") for the purpose of providing Customer with Web-based access to eGain's software specified in Exhibit A, including any updates, upgrades or revisions provided under this Agreement ("Software"), and certain other services relating to the processing of and response to online inquiries and messages ("Online Messages") received by Customer from its customers and other users of Customer's Web site ("Users").
rationale: Party and scope definitions are standard and impose no one-sided obligations on eGain.

text: This Agreement shall continue in effect from the Effective Date for a one (1) year period, unless earlier terminated as set forth below, and thereafter shall renew automatically for successive one (1) year periods unless either party gives the other party at least thirty (30) days prior written notice of its intent not to renew the Agreement.
rationale: Mutual non-renewal right with 30 days notice, "either party", is market-standard.

text: eGain grants Customers a non-exclusive, non-transferable, limited license, with right to sublicense solely to Users, to use such Software only in connection with the Hosting Services.
rationale: Limited, non-exclusive license "solely to Users" creates no meaningful risk to eGain's IP.

text: Customer agrees that, except as expressly set forth in this Section and in Section 11, it will not rent, lease, sublicense, re-sell, time-share or otherwise assign to any third party this Agreement or any of Customer's rights or licenses to access the Software or the eGain System, nor shall Customer use, or authorize others to use, the Software, Hosting Services or the eGain System to operate a service bureau.
rationale: Playbook requires consent of both parties; this restricts only Customer, "except as expressly set forth" in Section 11.

text: Except for the limited access right granted to Customer in this Agreement, all right, title and interest in and to the Software (including any and all modifications as a result of any implementation services rendered) and the eGain System are and shall remain the exclusive property of eGain and its licensors.
rationale: Software and eGain System stay "exclusive property of eGain"; no IP assigned to counterparty.

text: eGain acknowledges and agrees that the Online Messages are the property of Customer and that eGain has only a limited right to use the Online Messages as set forth in the following sentence.
rationale: Online Messages are Customer data, not eGain IP, so the no-assignment rule is not triggered.

text: At the end of the initial one-year term of this Agreement and any subsequent one-year terms, eGain may adjust the monthly fee payable under this Agreement by providing Customer written notice of such adjustment at least sixty (60) days prior to the beginning of the new term.
rationale: Only eGain may adjust fees, which favors the company; no adverse one-sided burden on eGain.

text: eGain represents and warrants that, prior to, during and after the calendar year 2000 A.D., the Software and the eGain System will process, calculate, manipulate, sort, store and transfer date data without material error or material performance degradation, including without limitation date data which represents or references different centuries or more than one century (such representation and warranty being referred to as "Year 2000 Compliant").
rationale: Warranty runs "prior to, during and after" 2000, an open-ended exposure that deviates from market practice.

text: eGain's entire liability under this Agreement for any damages from any cause whatsoever, regardless of form or action, whether in contract, negligence or otherwise, shall in no event exceed an amount equal to the price paid for the Services out of which the claim arose.
rationale: Cap protects only eGain, not both parties, and is "price paid for the Services", not 12 months' fees.

rationale: Rule: assignment requires consent of both parties. "without the prior written consent of the other party" matches the rule.

text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, no consent shall be required for an assignment of this Agreement made pursuant to a merger, consolidation, or the acquisition of all or substantially all of the business and assets of a party.
rationale: Rule: assignment requires prior written consent of both parties. "no consent shall be required" directly overrides the consent rule.

text: This agreement ("Agreement") is entered into as of the 23rd day of September, 1997 ("Effective Date"), by and between Excite, Inc., a California corporation, located at 555 Broadway, Redwood City, California 94063 ("Excite"), and N2K Inc., a Pennsylvania corporation, located at 55 Broad Street, 26th Floor, New York, New York, 10004 ("Sponsor").

text: The term of this Agreement will begin on the Effective Date and will end on the second (2nd) anniversary of the Commencement Date.

text: Sponsor will be the exclusive retail music store sponsor of the Excite Site and the Excite Broadcast Pages.
rationale: Exclusivity rule: "exclusive retail music store sponsor" requires business and legal approval before Excite commits.

text: Excite will not permit the display of advertising banners, promotional buttons, promotional links or other promotional materials for any retail sale of Music Products on the Excite Site, except those Music Products offered by Sponsor, nor advertising by any other Retail Music Store.

text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Excite may make available opportunities on the Excite Site to purchase Music Products from parties other than Sponsor if such Music Products are not available from Sponsor so long as, prior to entering into arrangements to make available opportunities to purchase Music Products from parties other than Sponsor, Excite notifies Sponsor of its interest in the Music Products and gives Sponsor thirty (30) days to make the desired Music Products available through the Sponsor Site.
rationale: One-sided rule: Excite must give Sponsor "thirty (30) days" notice and opportunity before sourcing elsewhere.

text: Excite will offer Sponsor the right of first refusal to negotiate with Excite for renewal of this sponsorship.
rationale: One-sided rule: "right of first refusal to negotiate" for renewal favors Sponsor and constrains Excite's options.

text: Excite will not propose, solicit or negotiate offers from entities other than Sponsor for any retail music store sponsorships of the Excite Site, if at all, until [****] prior to the expiration of the term of this Agreement.
rationale: Exclusivity rule: Excite "will not propose, solicit or negotiate" with other sponsors until bracketed pre-expiration date.

text: Commencing not later than [****] prior to the expiration of the term of the Agreement, Excite will negotiate with Sponsor in good faith with respect to the terms and conditions under which this Agreement would be renewed. Excite will negotiate exclusively with Sponsor for the next [****] in good faith effort to negotiate and execute a written sponsorship renewal agreement. If, [****] prior to the expiration of the term of the Agreement, the parties have not entered into a written sponsorship renewal agreement. Excite may enter into negotiations with any third party with respect to retail music store sponsorships of the Excite Site.
rationale: One-sided rule: Excite "will negotiate exclusively with Sponsor" and bars third-party talks until a bracketed deadline.

text: In the event that Excite intends to enter into an agreement with a third party with respect to retail music store sponsorships of the Excite Site before the expiration of the term of the Agreement, Excite will deliver to Sponsor a written notice describing the relevant opportunity.
rationale: One-sided rule: Excite must deliver "a written notice describing the relevant opportunity" to Sponsor before any third-party deal.

text: Sponsor will have [****] after receipt of such written notice to provide notice to Excite that it is prepared to enter into an agreement with Excite on the same terms and conditions as Excite proposes to accept from such third party.
rationale: One-sided rule: Sponsor gets matching right on "the same terms and conditions" within a bracketed period.

text: If Sponsor rejects said offer or fails to notify Excite of its acceptance within the [****] period, Excite shall have the right thereafter to enter into the agreement with such third party, provided the terms and conditions of the agreement (if entered into within the subsequent ninety (90) days) are not less favorable to Excite than previously offered by Sponsor.
rationale: One-sided rule: Excite may proceed with third party only if terms "not less favorable" within 90 days, limiting flexibility.

text: During the first year of the sponsorship following the Commencement Date, Excite will deliver not less than [****] Impressions on the Excite Site.
rationale: Minimum commitment rule: Excite "will deliver not less than" bracketed Impressions, a firm delivery obligation on Excite.

text: During the second year of the sponsorship following the first anniversary of the Commencement Date, Excite will deliver not less than [****] Impressions on the Excite Site.
rationale: Minimum commitment rule: Excite "will deliver not less than" bracketed Impressions in year two, a firm delivery obligation.

text: [****] will be due to Excite on the Effective Date as compensation for Excite's costs of initiating access to the Excite Site, programming costs, set-up costs and other expenses associated with Excite's initiation of the links, placements, advertisements and promotions contemplated by the Agreement.
Sponsor will pay Excite [****] per year as compensation for being the exclusive online retail music store sponsor of the Excite Site.
rationale: Exclusivity rule requires business and legal approval; clause grants "exclusive online retail music store sponsor" status for payment.

text: Sponsor will pay Excite a share of all gross margins Sponsor realizes on transactions, advertising, sponsorship, promotions and any other revenue generated during each year of the term of the Agreement on the Sponsor Site as a result of users referred from the Excite Site ("Total Revenue"), subject to the following conditions:
rationale: Flagged one-sided obligation: Sponsor shares "all gross margins" and "any other revenue," well beyond market practice.

text: Payments of shared gross margin will be due to Excite within thirty (30) days of the end of each calendar quarter in which the revenue is recognized by Sponsor.
rationale: Payment timing of thirty days after quarter end is a routine term, not a deviation from market practice.

text: Excite may, upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to Sponsor, cause an independent Certified Public Accountant to inspect the records of Sponsor reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during Sponsor's normal business hours.
rationale: Flagged one-sided right: only Excite may cause audit of Sponsor's "records," with no reciprocal right.

text: All data concerning users and their behavior relating to the use of the Excite Site will be owned solely by Excite.
rationale: Company data rule: user data is "owned solely by Excite," assigning Sponsor's user data to the counterparty.

text: Data relating to the use of the Co-Branded Pages will be jointly owned and shared by both parties.
rationale: Flagged for market deviation: Co-Branded Pages data "jointly owned and shared" could expose Sponsor's data use.

text: Sponsor will retain all right, title and interest in and to the Content worldwide (including, but not limited to, ownership of all copyrights and other intellectual property rights therein).
rationale: IP rule satisfied: Sponsor "will retain all right, title and interest" in its Content.

text: Excite will retain all right, title, and interest in and to the Excite Site and the Excite Network and the Broadcast Pages worldwide (including, but not limited to, ownership of all copyrights, look and feel and other intellectual property rights therein).
rationale: IP rule satisfied: Excite retains rights in its own site, not Sponsor's IP being assigned away.

text: Sponsor will retain all right, title and interest in and to its trademarks, service marks and trade names worldwide, subject to the limited license granted to Excite hereunder.
rationale: IP rule satisfied: Sponsor "will retain all right, title and interest" in its trademarks, subject to limited license.

text: Excite will retain all right, title and interest in and to its trademarks, service marks and trade names worldwide, subject to the limited license granted to Sponsor hereunder.
rationale: IP rule satisfied: Excite retains its own trademarks, subject to limited license to Sponsor.

text: Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, Sponsor hereby grants to Excite a royalty-free, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use, reproduce, distribute, transmit and publicly display the Content in accordance with this Agreement and to sub-license the Content to Excite's wholly-owned subsidiaries or to joint ventures in which Excite participates for the sole purpose of using, reproducing, distributing, transmitting and publicly displaying the Content in accordance with this Agreement
rationale: Flagged one-sided grant: royalty-free, worldwide license of Sponsor's Content, sublicensable to Excite's subsidiaries and joint ventures.

text: Each party hereby grants to the other a non-exclusive, limited license to use its trademarks, service marks or trade names only as specifically described in this Agreement.
rationale: Reciprocal, non-exclusive, limited trademark license "only as specifically described" is balanced and market-standard.

text: Neither party may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without the other party's written consent (which will not be unreasonably withheld), except that no such consent will be required in connection with (i) a merger, reorganization or sale of all, or substantially all, of such party's assets or (ii) either party's assignment and/or delegation of its rights and responsibilities hereunder to a wholly-owned subsidiary or joint venture in which such party holds a controlling interest. Any attempt to assign this Agreement other than as permitted above will be null and void.

text: This Agreement will be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York
rationale: New York governing law is mutual and common market practice; no one-sided obligation is created.

text: THE LIABILITY OF EXCITE FOR DAMAGES OR ALLEGED DAMAGES HEREUNDER, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, TORT OR ANY OTHER LEGAL THEORY, IS LIMITED TO, AND WILL NOT EXCEED, THE AMOUNTS ACTUALLY PAID BY SPONSOR TO EXCITE HEREUNDER.
rationale: Rule requires a mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees; this caps only 'LIABILITY OF EXCITE' at 'AMOUNTS ACTUALLY PAID'.

text: Licensor on behalf of itself and its Affliates hereby grants to Licensee the limited licenses to use and have used the Licensed Mark: (i) for the Licensed Products as set forth on Schedule 2; and (ii) as set forth on Schedule 1, concerning agreements entered into by Licensee prior to the Effective Date ("Existing Agreements").

text: For the avoidance of doubt, Licensor also grants to Licensee and its subsidiaries and affiliates a non-exclusive, worldwide royalty-free license for continued use of the Licensed Mark for the production and sale of inventory containing the Licensed Mark applied to such products during the Transition Period as set forth in section 8.2 of the Separation and Distribution Agreement and in Schedule 2 of this Agreement.

text: For avoidance of doubt, to the extent that any of the licenses granted by the terms of this Agreement include any right to sublicense, such right to sublicense shall extend to Licensee's subsidiaries and joint venturers.
