rationale: Playbook rule: flag deviations or one-sided obligations. Date "June 25, 2014" is a plain fact with no deviation.

text: MASTER FRANCHISE AGREEMENT
rationale: Title only; no substantive term to deviate from playbook rules.

text: AGREEMENT made as of the _____ day of __________________, 2015 (the "Effective Date") by and between Kiosk Concepts, Inc., a New York corporation having its principal place of business at 1110 South Avenue, Staten Island, New York 10314 ("we", "us" or "our"), and The Grilled Cheese Truck, Inc., a Nevada corporation having its principal address at 151 North Nob Hill Road, Suite 321, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33324 ("you" or "your"), with reference to the following facts:
rationale: Standard party identification; no deviation from market practice or one-sided obligations.

text: The initial term of this Agreement shall commence upon the Effective Date and shall expire ten (10) years from the Effective Date, unless sooner terminated under the terms of this Agreement.
rationale: Ten-year initial term "shall expire ten (10) years" is within typical market range.

text: You shall have no right or option to extend or renew the term of this Agreement except as provided in Section 3.2 of this Agreement.
rationale: "no right or option to extend or renew" except Section 3.2, which grants a renewal option; limited exposure.

text: You shall have the option to renew the term of this Agreement, on the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement, for four (4) additional ten (10) year terms, upon written notice given by you to us not less than six (6) months nor more than twelve (12) months prior to the scheduled expiration date of the term then in effect, provided that each of the following conditions are satisfied:
rationale: Franchisee renewal option for "four (4) additional ten (10) year terms" is favorable, though conditions are truncated.

text: You shall, at our option, execute our then-current form of Master Franchise Agreement and any addenda thereto for the renewal term, which renewal agreement shall supersede this Agreement in all respects, and the terms of which, including, without limitation, continuing fees payable to us, may differ materially and be less advantageous to you than the terms of this Agreement.
rationale: Playbook one-sided terms: "at our option" and "may differ materially and be less advantageous to you."

text: We grant to you, upon the terms and conditions contained in this Agreement, the exclusive right to establish and operate a Franchised Business and a license to use the methods, procedures and products developed by us in the business of selling and servicing Unit Franchises in the territory described on Attachment A attached to this Agreement and incorporated into this Agreement by reference (the "Master Territory").
rationale: Playbook requires approval for exclusive arrangements; "exclusive right" grant needs business and legal sign-off.

text: The rights granted herein include the limited right to sublicense the use of the Proprietary Marks to Unit Franchisees in the Master Territory.
rationale: "limited right to sublicense the use of the Proprietary Marks" to unit franchisees is standard for master franchise deals.

text: You acknowledge and agree that the franchise granted to you hereunder is non-exclusive and is only for one (1) Master Territory; that you are not granted any area, market, or protected territorial rights other than as expressly provided in Section 1.1 of this Agreement; and that you shall not have the right to sublicense, sublease, subcontract or enter into any management agreement providing for the right to operate the Franchised Business or to use the System granted pursuant to this Agreement, except in the manner expressly provided for in Section 5.1 of this Agreement.
rationale: Bars "sublicense, sublease, subcontract" except per Section 5.1; restricts us, lacks mutual consent language.

text: 1.3.2 To own, acquire, establish and/or operate, and license others to establish and operate, businesses under other proprietary marks or other systems, whether such businesses are the same, similar, or different from the Franchised Business, at any location within or outside of the Master Territory.
rationale: Reserved right to "operate... at any location within or outside of the Master Territory" undermines the exclusive grant.

text: You shall pay us a renewal fee in the sum of Ten Thousand Dollars ($10,000) for the right to renew this Agreement.
rationale: Flat "renewal fee" of $10,000 for renewal rights is a one-sided payment that departs from typical renewal terms.

text: If we are not offering new master franchises, are in the process of revising, amending or renewing our form of Master Franchise Agreement or Master Franchise Disclosure Document or are not lawfully able to offer our then-current form of Master Franchise Agreement at the time you exercise an option to extend the term of this Agreement, we may offer to renew this Agreement upon the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement for the extended term, or may offer to extend the term of this Agreement on a month-to-month basis following the expiration of the term of this Agreement for as long as we deem necessary or appropriate so that we may subsequently lawfully offer and utilize our then-current form of Master Franchise Agreement.
rationale: Franchisor may extend month-to-month "for as long as we deem necessary"; open-ended, one-sided discretion deviating from market practice.

text: Your right to extend the term of this Agreement shall be subject to your continued compliance with the terms and conditions in this Agreement as well as your compliance with the conditions set forth in Section 3.2 of this Agreement.
rationale: Extension right is "subject to your continued compliance" plus Section 3.2 conditions; one-sided conditions on franchisee.

text: If you do not elect to extend the term of this Agreement, this Agreement shall terminate at the end of the term then in effect.
rationale: Standard expiration: agreement terminates at term end unless franchisee elects extension. Consistent with market practice.

text: You shall execute a general release, in a form prescribed by us, of any and all claims which you may have or believe to have against us and/or our affiliates and our respective officers, directors, agents and employees, whether the claims are known or unknown, which are based on, arise from or relate to this Agreement or the Franchised Business, as well as claims, known or unknown, which are not based on, do not arise from or do not relate to this Agreement or the Franchised Business, but which relate to other franchise agreements, Franchised Businesses and other agreements between us or our affiliates and you which arose on or before the date of the general release, including, without limitation, all obligations, liabilities, demands, costs, expenses, damages, claims, actions and causes of action, of whatever nature, character or description, arising under federal, state and local laws, rules and ordinances (provided, however, that all rights enjoyed by you and any causes of action arising in your favor from the provisions of Article 33 of the New York General Business Law ("GBL") and the regulations issued thereunder shall remain in force; it being the intent of this provision that the non-waiver provisions of GBL Sections 687.4 and 687.5 be satisfied).
rationale: Rule: waivers of legal remedies need legal approval. "general release... known or unknown" waives broad claims, including unrelated agreements.

text: You shall pay to us a royalty fee based on revenue generated by Unit Franchisees (the "Unit Franchise Performance Royalty Fee") equal to twenty-five percent (25%) of aggregate royalty fees paid to you by Unit Franchisees in the Master Territory pursuant to their Unit Franchise Agreements.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. "twenty-five percent (25%) of aggregate royalty fees" from unit franchisees is an unusually large share.

text: You shall pay to us a franchise sales royalty fee (the "Franchise Sales Royalty Fee") for each Unit Franchise you sell in the Master Territory as follows: twenty-five percent (25%) of the initial franchise fee collected from each Unit Franchisee upon execution of the Unit Franchisee's Franchise Agreement (a "Unit Franchise Agreement"); provided, however, that if you elect to discount or reduce an initial franchise fee for any reason, the Franchise Sales Royalty Fee shall be payable to us as if the full initial franchise fee had been paid.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. "twenty-five percent (25%)" of initial fee, owed even if discounted "as if the full initial franchise fee had been paid."

text: Fees and Royalties cannot be increased or decreased without our prior written consent.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. Fees "cannot be increased or decreased without our prior written consent" restricts franchisee pricing control.

text: (b) Soups shall be cost plus 25% FOB the supplier.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. "cost plus 25%" markup on soups, fixed by franchisor, limits franchisee margin.

text: (d) In order to keep your exclusivity, you agree to purchase a minimum of the following:   $170,000.00 of soup from us in 2015 $1,600,00.00 of soup from us in 2016 $3,200,000.00 of soup from us in 2017 $5,000,000.00 of soup from us in 2018 and shall increase 10% each year thereafter.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. Escalating minimums "increase 10% each year thereafter"; amounts also contain a typo ("$1,600,00.00").

text: (e) We maintain the right to open and operate new company units and to sell franchises to our existing franchisees.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. Franchisor may "open and operate new company units" and sell to existing franchisees, undercutting exclusivity.

text: We shall be permitted to sell branded products to national accounts without any money due to you or your parent company.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "without any money due to you" favors the company; minor franchisee-relations risk only.

text: Once you have units open and operating in the trade area where a National Account is located, we will remit to you 25% of the profits derived from the sales in that specific trade area.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "we will remit to you 25% of the profits" creates open-ended company payout exposure, deviating from market practice.

text: In addition to The Original Soupman business you must own and continuously operate, you must sell and have open the minimum number of The Original Soupman businesses as set forth on Attachment E hereto (the "Minimum Development Quota") by the dates set forth on such Attachment.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "Minimum Development Quota" obligates the franchisee and protects the company's development plans.

text: We will not grant other franchises nor establish our own Unit Franchises within the Master Territory during the term of this Agreement unless you do not meet the Minimum Development Quota.
rationale: Rule: exclusive arrangements need approval. "We will not grant other franchises" is a company exclusivity commitment requiring business and legal sign-off.

text: If you do not meet the Minimum Development Quota, we may cancel your exclusive right to market and sell Unit Franchises in your Master Territory and may sell additional Master Franchises within your Master Territory, or we may begin operations of our own in your Master Territory, or we may terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Rule: exclusive arrangements. "we may cancel your exclusive right" gives the company broad remedies on franchisee quota shortfall.

text: You must charge your Unit Franchisees the initial franchise fee, royalty fee, National Advertising Fund Contribution and any other continuing fees that we designate or require, within the limits established by all regulatory agencies which now or hereafter may have jurisdiction over the sale of franchises and the requirements imposed by this Agreement. Any deviations from these amounts must be pre- approved by us.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "fees that we designate" with pre-approval for deviations raises resale price restriction and regulatory exposure.

text: During the term of this Agreement, you shall maintain in force under policies of insurance issued by licensed insurers approved by us insurance coverage as we from time to time require.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "coverage as we from time to time require" favors the company's flexibility; franchisee bears the cost.

text: As it relates to the operation of your Franchised Business: broad form comprehensive general liability coverage against claims for employment practices coverage, bodily and personal injury, death and property damage caused by or occurring in conjunction with the conduct of business by you pursuant to this Agreement and broad form contractual liability coverage, including errors and omissions coverage, under one or more policies of insurance containing minimum liability coverage prescribed by us from time to time, but in no event in an amount less than Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000) aggregate. Such insurance shall not have a deductible or self-insured retention in excess of Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000);
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "not less than Two Million Dollars" and deductible cap of "$5,000" are protective and reasonable.

text: As it relates to the operation of your Franchised Business: automobile liability insurance coverage, including owned and non-owned vehicles, with limits of not less than One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence;
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "not less than One Million Dollars ($1,000,000)" auto coverage is a standard, protective requirement.

text: As it relates to the operation of your Franchised Business: worker's compensation and employer's liability insurance in statutory amounts, unemployment insurance and state disability insurance as required by governing law for your employees;
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "statutory amounts" and "as required by governing law" are standard, legally compliant requirements.

text: You acknowledge and agree that any such concept, process or improvement shall become our property and we may utilize or disclose such information to other master franchisees and unit franchisees as we determine to be appropriate.
rationale: Playbook bars assigning company IP to counterparty; clause says "shall become our property" for counterparty concepts, and we may disclose them to others, which is a company-favorable transfer to the company but flags assignment-type language.

text: We shall own all intellectual property and other rights in the System Website and all information it contains, including the domain name or uniform resource locator ("URL") for the System Website, the log of "hits" by visitors, and any personal or business data that visitors (including you and your personnel) supply.
rationale: Clause keeps IP with the company ("We shall own all intellectual property"), consistent with the rule that company IP may not be assigned to the counterparty.

text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, we reserve the right to inspect or examine your accounts, books, records and tax returns, at any reasonable time, with or without prior notice to you.
rationale: Playbook flags one-sided terms; "at any reasonable time, with or without prior notice" and tax returns is broad, one-sided audit access.

text: You further acknowledge and agree that we may inspect your Franchised Business and any Unit Franchise in the Master Territory to verify that your Franchised Business and/or such Unit Franchise is operating in compliance with our System, as it may be modified from time to time.
rationale: Playbook flags one-sided terms; "we may inspect" with no notice or frequency limits, and the "as it may be modified from time to time" System standard shifts risk to counterparty.

text: You shall expend not less than $5,000 each month on such Solicitation Advertising.
rationale: Playbook flags one-sided obligations; fixed "not less than $5,000 each month" minimum spend is a firm, unilateral commitment that deviates from market practice.

text: In consideration for such training, trade secrets and confidential information, you and your principals agree that during the term of this Agreement, and for a continuous uninterrupted period commencing upon expiration or termination of this Agreement, regardless of the cause for termination, and continuing for a period of three (3) years thereafter, neither you nor your principals shall, directly or indirectly, for themselves, or through, on behalf of, or in conjunction with any person, persons, partnership, limited liability company or corporation:
rationale: Non-compete binds franchisee, not company; rule targets restrictions on company's business activity, so no company exposure.

text: Divert or attempt to divert any business or customer of the Franchised Business or any Unit Franchisee anywhere, by direct or indirect inducement or otherwise, or do or perform, directly or indirectly, any other act injurious or prejudicial to the goodwill associated with our Proprietary Marks or the System.
rationale: Customer no-solicit restricts only the franchisee and protects company goodwill; consistent with market practice.

text: Employ or seek to employ any person who is at that time employed by us or by any other master franchisee or unit franchisee in the System, or otherwise directly or indirectly induce such person to leave his or her employment without our written consent.
rationale: Employee no-solicit is one-sided and reaches other franchisees' employees with no time limit, risking deviation from market practice.

text: Own, maintain, operate, engage in, or have any interest in any business which is the same as or similar to the Franchised Business, or any other business which performs any type of child tutoring services, anywhere.
rationale: Restricts franchisee's business 'anywhere' across broad tutoring scope; one-sided and possibly unenforceable, creating legal exposure.

text: Each of the foregoing covenants shall be construed as independent of any other covenant or provision of this Agreement. If all or any portion of any covenant in this Section 7 is held unreasonable or unenforceable by a court having valid jurisdiction in any unappealed final decision to which we are a party, you and your principals shall be bound by any lesser covenant subsumed within the terms of such covenant that imposes the maximum duty permitted by law, as if the resulting covenant were separately stated in and made a part of this Section 7.
The right and license of the Proprietary Marks granted under this Agreement to you is non-exclusive, and we and our affiliates have and retain the rights described in Section 1.3 of this Agreement.
rationale: Non-exclusive license with company retaining rights is company-favorable and does not assign company IP away.

text: Nothing in the Franchise Agreement shall limit our right to maintain websites other than the System Website or to offer and sell products and services under the Marks from the System Website, another website or otherwise over the Internet without payment or obligation of any kind to you.
rationale: Non-exclusive reservation lets company sell online without obligation; no exclusive arrangement is granted to franchisee.

text: We alone will be, and at all times will remain, the sole owner of the copyrights to all material which appears on any System Website we establish and maintain, including any and all material you may furnish to us as provided above.
rationale: 'We alone will be... the sole owner of the copyrights' keeps company IP with company, including franchisee-furnished material.

text: You shall, at our option and request, and without any additional consideration, assign to us all rights to all e-mail addresses, URLs, domain names, Internet listings, and Internet accounts related to the Franchised Business following demand by us upon your misuse of the same and/or the termination or expiration of this Agreement.
rationale: Domain and account assignment runs to company, not to counterparty, so the 'may not be assigned to counterparty' rule is not triggered.

text: As between you and us, we are the owner of all right, title, and interest in and to the Proprietary Marks and the goodwill associated with and symbolized by them and we have the right to use, and license others to use, the Proprietary Marks.
rationale: 'we are the owner of all right, title, and interest' in the Proprietary Marks; company retains ownership and licensing rights.

text: Every covenant required by this Section 7.6 shall be in a form satisfactory to us, including, without limitation, specific identification of us as a third party beneficiary of such covenants with an independent right to enforce them.
rationale: Rule flags one-sided terms. "Every covenant... satisfactory to us" plus independent enforcement right for franchisor only is one-sided.

text: Such covenants shall be in a form satisfactory to us, including, without limitation, specific identification of us as a third party beneficiary of such covenants with the independent right to enforce them.
rationale: Rule flags one-sided terms. "satisfactory to us" and franchisor-only independent enforcement right is one-sided, though narrower in scope.

text: If any purported assignment or transfer of any direct or indirect interest in this Agreement, in you, or in all or substantially all of the assets of the Franchised Business is made to any third party without our prior written consent, contrary to the terms of Section 12 of this Agreement.
rationale: Rule requires consent of both parties. Clause requires only "our prior written consent," a one-sided deviation.

text: If you fail to obtain or maintain required insurance coverage and do not obtain such coverage within ten (10) days after written notice from us.
rationale: Rule flags one-sided or off-market terms. "within ten (10) days after written notice" gives a standard cure period.

text: If you fail to comply with the Minimum Development Quota.
rationale: Rule flags one-sided obligations. "fail to comply with the Minimum Development Quota" triggers breach with no cure period.

text: You shall have no right to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Termination for convenience rule: clause says "no right to terminate" for counterparty, stricter than the 90-day minimum.

text: In addition to the foregoing, upon termination of this Agreement by us for cause as described in Section 10, you agree to pay to us within fifteen (15) days after the effective date of this Agreement's termination, in addition to the amounts owed hereunder, liquidated damages equal to the average monthly Unit Franchise Performance Royalty Fee and Franchise Sales Royalty Fee you paid during the twelve (12) months of operation preceding the effective date of termination multiplied by (a) twenty-four (24) (being the number of months in two (2) full years), or (b) the number of months remaining in the Agreement had it not been terminated, whichever is lower.
rationale: Liquidated damages rule: "liquidated damages" is a pre-set penalty requiring legal approval; none is shown.

text: The parties hereto acknowledge and agree that it would be impracticable to determine precisely the damages we would incur from this Agreement's termination and the loss of cash flow from Royalty Fees due to, among other things, the complications of determining what costs, if any, we might have saved and how much the Royalty Fees would have grown over what would have been this Agreement's remaining term. The parties hereto consider this liquidated damages provision to be a reasonable, good faith pre-estimate of those damages.
rationale: Liquidated damages rule: "reasonable, good faith pre-estimate" is a pre-set damages term requiring legal approval; none is shown.

text: The liquidated damages provision only covers our damages from the loss of cash flow from the Royalty Fees. It does not cover any other damages, including damages to our reputation with the public and landlords and damages arising from a violation of any provision of this Agreement other than the Royalty Fee sections. You and each of your principals agree that the liquidated damages provision does not give us an adequate remedy at law for any default under, or for the enforcement of, any provision of this Agreement other than the Royalty Fee sections.
rationale: Liquidated damages rule: "does not give us an adequate remedy at law" narrows company remedies and still requires legal approval.

text: We shall have the right to assign this Agreement and all of our attendant rights and privileges to any person, firm, corporation or other entity provided that, with respect to any assignment resulting in the subsequent performance by the assignee of our functions: (i) the assignee shall, at the time of such assignment, be financially responsible and economically capable of performing our obligations; and (ii) the assignee shall expressly assume and agree to perform such obligations.
rationale: Mutual-consent assignment rule: "We shall have the right to assign" without franchisee consent departs from the playbook requirement.

text: You expressly affirm and agree that we may sell our assets, our rights to the Proprietary Marks or to the System outright to a third party; may go public; may engage in a private placement of some or all of our securities; may merge, acquire other corporations, or be acquired by another corporation; may undertake a refinancing, recapitalization, leveraged buyout or other economic or financial restructuring; and, with regard to any or all of the above sales, assignments and dispositions, you expressly and specifically waive any claims, demands or damages arising from or related to the loss of said Proprietary Marks (or any variation thereof) and/or the loss of association with or identification of "Kiosk Concepts, Inc." as Franchisor.
rationale: Change of control rule: counterparty gets no termination or renegotiation right; "expressly and specifically waive" favors company.

text: neither you nor any immediate or remote successor to any part of your interest in this Agreement, nor any individual, partnership, corporation, or other legal entity which directly or indirectly owns any interest in you shall not sell, encumber, assign, transfer, convey, pledge, merge, or give away any direct or indirect interest in this Agreement, in you, or in all or substantially all of the assets of the Franchised Business.
rationale: Assignment rule: restricts franchisee transfers, including owners' interests, which favors company; drafting double negative needs cleanup.

text: Any change in the control of you shall be deemed a transfer for purposes of this Agreement.
rationale: Change of control rule: "deemed a transfer" gives company consent leverage; no counterparty termination right is created.

text: Any purported assignment or transfer shall be null and void and shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement, for which we may immediately terminate without opportunity to cure pursuant to Section 10.2.3 of this Agreement.
rationale: Assignment rule: "null and void" and immediate termination without cure strongly protect company; no exposure identified.

text: You shall not grant a security interest in the Franchised Business or in any of the assets of the Franchised Business without first obtaining our prior written consent.
rationale: Assignment rule: "without first obtaining our prior written consent" applies only to franchisee, favoring company.

text: Upon the death or permanent disability (mental or physical) of any person with an interest in this Agreement, in you, or in all or substantially all of the assets of the Franchised Business, the executor, administrator, or personal representative of such person shall transfer such interest to a third party approved by us within twelve (12) months after such death or disability.
rationale: Assignment rule: "approved by us" keeps buyer control with company; the 12-month transfer window is a minor continuity concern.

text: To Franchisor: Kiosk Concepts, Inc.
rationale: Playbook one-sided rule: 'To Franchisor: Kiosk Concepts, Inc.' is a plain party identification with no obligations.

text: To Master Franchisee: The Grilled Cheese Truck, Inc.
rationale: Playbook one-sided rule: 'To Master Franchisee' is a plain party identification with no obligations.

text: If, for any reason, this Agreement is not terminated pursuant to Section 10.1 and this Agreement is assumed, or assignment of the same to any person or entity who has made a bona fide offer to accept an assignment of this Agreement is contemplated pursuant to the United States Bankruptcy Code, then notice of such proposed assignment or assumption setting forth: (a) the name and address of the proposed assignee, and (b) all of the terms and conditions of the proposed assignment and assumption shall be given to us within twenty (20) days after receipt of such proposed assignee's offer to accept assignment of this Agreement, and, in any event, within ten (10) days prior to the date application is made to a court of competent jurisdiction for authority and approval to enter into such assignment and assumption, and we shall thereupon have the prior right and option, to be exercised by notice given at any time prior to the effective date of such proposed assignment and assumption, to accept an assignment of this Agreement to us upon the same terms and conditions and for the same consideration, if any, as in the bona fide offer made by the proposed assignee, less any brokerage commissions which may be payable by you out of the consideration to be paid by such assignee for the assignment of this Agreement.
rationale: Playbook one-sided rule: franchisor gets a 'prior right and option' to take assignment in bankruptcy, with short 'twenty (20) days' notice windows.

text: You and we acknowledge and agree that we are a third-party beneficiary to all Unit Franchise Agreements between you and Unit Franchisees in the Master Territory, and that we shall have the right to assume any of your responsibilities, duties or functions under such Unit Franchise Agreements in the event that this Agreement expires or is terminated for any reason.
rationale: Playbook one-sided rule: franchisor may 'assume any of your responsibilities, duties or functions' under unit agreements on termination, a major one-sided exposure.

text: You shall include in the standard Unit Franchise Agreement used by you a provision which states that we are a third-party beneficiary to the Unit Franchise Agreement and are entitled to the rights granted in this Section 13.
rationale: Playbook one-sided rule: requires company to include 'third-party beneficiary' provision in every unit agreement, an operational burden favoring franchisor.

text: We shall have the right, but not the obligation, to enforce any provision of any Unit Franchise Agreement if you fail to properly and promptly do so.
rationale: Playbook one-sided rule: franchisor may enforce unit agreements 'if you fail to properly and promptly do so,' with no reciprocal obligation.

text: This Agreement shall be interpreted and construed under the laws of the State of New York. In the event of any conflict of law, the laws of New York shall prevail, without regard to the application of such state's conflict of law rules. If, however, any provision of this Agreement would not be enforceable under the laws of New York, and if the Franchised Business is located outside of New York and such provision would be enforceable under the laws of the state in which the Franchised Business is located, then such provision shall be interpreted and construed under the laws of that other state. Nothing in this Section 17.1 is intended by the parties to subject this Agreement to laws, rules, or regulation of any state to which it would not otherwise be subject.
rationale: Playbook flags deviation from market practice: NY law with conflict-of-law override and fallback to franchisee's state, "shall prevail", adds uncertainty.

text: The term "Master Franchisee" or "you" as used in this Agreement shall refer to each person executing this Agreement as Master Franchisee/you, whether such person is one of the spouses, partners, shareholders, members, trustees, trustors or beneficiaries or persons named as included in Master Franchisee/you, and shall apply to each such person as if he were the only named Master Franchisee in this Agreement.
rationale: Playbook flags one-sided obligations; this clause binds each named person "as if he were the only named" franchisee, which favors the company.

text: IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement on the date first shown above.
KIOSK CONCEPTS, INC.:
rationale: Party name header only; no obligations or one-sided terms appear in "KIOSK CONCEPTS, INC."

text: MASTER FRANCHISEE :       THE GRILLED CHEESE TRUCK, INC.
rationale: Party identification only; "MASTER FRANCHISEE" creates no obligations or one-sided terms.

text: COMMENCEMENT DATE: Upon approval of the State of New York.
rationale: Playbook flags non-market terms; "Upon approval of the State of New York" makes the start date contingent on an uncertain external approval.

text: each is limited to recovering only the actual damages proven to have been sustained by it.
rationale: Playbook requires a cap of at least 12 months' fees; "limited to recovering only the actual damages" sets no fee-based cap.

text: Attachment A to  Master Franchise Agreement
rationale: Document title only; "Attachment A to Master Franchise Agreement" contains no substantive terms.

text: PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT AND CO-BRANDING AGREEMENT
rationale: Rule: market practice. "PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT AND CO-BRANDING AGREEMENT" is a neutral title with no deviating terms.

text: This Agreement, entered into this the 10th day of January 2000, by and between INTEGRITY INCORPORATED, a Delaware corporation with principal offices at 1000 Cody Road, Mobile, Alabama ("Integrity") and TIME LIFE, INC., a Delaware corporation d/b/a Time Life Music, with principal offices located at 2000 Duke Street, Alexandria, Virginia 22314 ("TL").
rationale: Rule: market practice. Standard party identification with no one-sided terms in "by and between" language.

text: TL will hold exclusive worldwide rights to promote and sell the product through the following distribution channels: Outgoing telemarketing, General Market retail, and General Market catalogs, and exclusive rights within the United States for Television Direct response.
rationale: Rule: exclusive arrangements need approval. "exclusive worldwide rights" to TL requires business and legal sign-off.

text: Integrity will hold exclusive worldwide rights to promote and sell the product to/through the following distribution channels: Christian retail (CBA or Christian Booksellers Association markets), direct mail (including continuity sales, church sales, digital and e-commerce sales.)
rationale: Rule: exclusive arrangements need approval. "exclusive worldwide rights" to Integrity across channels requires business and legal sign-off.

text: (i.e., television and direct response will have a period of exclusivity before the products are available at retail).
rationale: Rule: exclusive arrangements need approval. "period of exclusivity before the products are available at retail" requires approval.

text: Mechanical rates will not exceed [**]/1/ percent ([**]/1/%) of the then-current statutory rate, and Print licenses will not exceed a prorated portion of [**]/1/ percent ([**]/1/%) of the retail selling price, Integrity will also manufacture the Product and sell to TL its requirements for resale.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "Integrity will also manufacture the Product and sell to TL its requirements" creates a supply obligation and rate caps.

text: The parties agree that the initial suggested retail selling price for the products will be $19.95 for CD's, $17.95 for Cassettes, and $19.95 for song books. Any change in the suggested retail selling price will be mutually agreed by the parties.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "Any change ... will be mutually agreed" keeps pricing balanced.

text: In consideration of the above pricing, TL guarantees to purchase from Integrity a minimum of ten thousand (10,000) units of each recorded Product during the first thirty-two (32) months of release.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "TL guarantees to purchase ... a minimum of ten thousand (10,000) units" binds TL to volume.

text: TL's initial order for each recorded Product shall be a minimum of five thousand (5,000) units.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "initial order ... shall be a minimum of five thousand (5,000) units" is a firm purchase floor.

text: TL may purchase from Integrity limited quantities of the Product for its promotional use, at the Manufacturing cost set forth in paragraph 3(a) above, provided the quantity of such purchases does not exceed seven percent (7%) of the total royalty bearing units of such Product title purchased by TL,
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "does not exceed seven percent (7%)" is a modest, mutually understood promotional cap.

text: On sales of recorded products pursuant to this Agreement (less any returns) Integrity will pay to TL royalties in the amount of [**]/1/ ($[**]/1/) for each and every unit of the product sold by Integrity in the United States pursuant to this Agreement, and [**]/1/ the foregoing rate or [**]/1/ percent ([**]/1/%) of Integrity's net receipts, whichever is less, on subject products outside the United States.
rationale: Rule: revenue sharing. Royalty amounts are redacted "[**]" and foreign rate "whichever is less" cannot be verified.

text: On sales of printed products (song books) pursuant to this Agreement (less any returns) Integrity will pay to TL royalties in the amount of [**]/1/ ($[**]/1/) for each and every unit of the product sold by Integrity in the United States pursuant to this Agreement, and [**]/1/ the foregoing rate or [**]/1/ percent ([**]/1/%) of Integrity's net receipts, whichever is less, on subject products outside the United States.
rationale: Rule: revenue sharing. Song book royalty amounts are redacted "[**]" and cannot be verified against market practice.

text: On sales of products pursuant to this Agreement (less any returns) TL will pay to Integrity royalties in the amount of [**]/1/ ($[**]/1/) for each and every unit of the product sold by it pursuant to this Agreement.
rationale: Rule: revenue sharing. TL's royalty to Integrity is redacted "[**]" so the payment terms cannot be verified.

text: Either party, at its sole expense, upon at least thirty (30) days written notice (and not more than once in respect of any accounting period) will have the right to inspect the other party's books regarding the obligations hereunder for a period of two (2) years from the date on which any statement is rendered.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "Either party" with "at its sole expense" and once per period is mutual and standard.

text: Such auditing party must make specific written objection within such two (2) year period.
rationale: Rule: market practice. "Such auditing party must make specific written objection within such two (2) year period" is mutual and workable.

text: Provided the objecting party has made timely written objection, as aforesaid, such party may file an action regarding same within two (2) years and six (6) months after the applicable statement is rendered, after which time any such action will be deemed barred.
rationale: Rule: deviates from market practice. "within two (2) years and six (6) months" shortens the dispute window and bars later actions.

text: Integrity hereby grants to TL the right to use its "Integrity Music" name and logo ("the Integrity Trademarks') in connection with the products produced during the Term of this Agreement for as long as the parties continue to sell and distribute such products at no additional cost to TL, and in accordance with the terms and conditions contained herein.
rationale: Rule: deviates from market practice. Trademark license runs "for as long as" products sell "at no additional cost to TL," with one-way grant.

text: TL hereby grants to Integrity the right to use its "TL Music" name and logo ("the TL Trademarks") in connection with the products produced during the Term of this Agreement for as long as the parties continue to sell and distribute such products at no additional cost to Integrity, and in accordance with the terms and conditions contained herein.
rationale: Rule: deviates from market practice. Mirror trademark license "at no additional cost to Integrity" with open-ended duration tied to sales.

text: The parties hereby agree that the copyright in the Product sound recording compilation will be jointly registered by Integrity in the names of Integrity and TL.
rationale: Rule: deviates from market practice. Copyright "jointly registered by Integrity in the names of Integrity and TL" creates co-ownership and control issues.

text: TL will trademark the series name in joint names of TL and Integrity.
rationale: Rule: deviates from market practice. Series trademark held "in joint names of TL and Integrity," creating shared enforcement and ownership complexity.

text: This agreement shall commence as of date first above written, and shall Continue through December 31, 2004 ("the Term").
rationale: Rule: deviates from market practice. "through December 31, 2004" is a fixed, definite end date, which is standard.

text: Thereafter, the parties must mutually agree in writing to extend the term for additional periods of time.
rationale: Rule: one-sided obligations. "the parties must mutually agree in writing to extend" is balanced and mutual.

text: Either party may, at its election, assign this Agreement or any of its rights or delegate any of its obligations hereunder, in whole or in part, to any person, firm or corporation owning or acquiring all or a substantial portion of its assets, to any person, firm or corporation that is related to it as an affiliate,
rationale: Rule: requires prior written consent of both parties. "Either party may, at its election, assign" without consent, including to acquirers.

text: assignment by either party of its rights to an unrelated third party, the other party shall be given written notice, then in such event the other party may upon six-months (6-months) written notice terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Rule: requires prior written consent of both parties. "assignment ... to an unrelated third party" needs only notice, not consent.

text: This Agreement has been entered into in the State of Tennessee, and the validity, interpretation and legal effect of this Agreement will be governed by the laws of the State of Tennessee applicable to contracts entered into and performed entirely within the State of Tennessee.
rationale: Rule: deviates from market practice. Tennessee governing law is neutral and applies to both parties equally.

text: Oceanic Time Warner Cable and Watchit Media Content and License Agreement
rationale: Playbook rule on deviations from market practice: document title "Media Content and License Agreement" is standard and creates no one-sided obligation.

text: Effective Dates: September 1, 2006, August 31, 2007
rationale: Playbook rule on deviations from market practice: "September 1, 2006, August 31, 2007" is a standard one-year term.

text: Oceanic Time Warner Cable will use the content solely on channel 777, the Las Vegas channel.
rationale: Playbook rule on one-sided obligations: "solely on channel 777" narrows use and is not an unusual burden.

text: In the event that Oceanic Time Warner Cable removes the above content and or terminates this agreement prior to December 31, 2006, Oceanic Time Warner Cable agrees to pay a cancellation fee of Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000) per month multiplied by the number of months remain on the agreement.
rationale: Playbook rule requires legal approval for pre-set damages: "cancellation fee of Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000) per month".

text: Watchit shall have the exclusive right to sell third party advertising as sponsors of their content and will have the right to brand the content under the Watchit brand and place a "bug" on the screen identifying the content with a Watchit trademark.
rationale: Playbook rule requires business and legal approval for exclusivity: "exclusive right to sell third party advertising".

text: This agreement will be in effect until the end of 2006 and will be evaluated at that time.
rationale: Playbook rule on market deviations: "until the end of 2006" conflicts with the August 31, 2007 end date in the effective dates.

text: THIS AGREEMENT (the "AGREEMENT") entered into as of the 19 day of March, 2004 (the "EFFECTIVE DATE") provides the terms and conditions under which MediaNet Group Technologies, Inc., a Nevada corporation having an address at 5100 W. Copans Road Suite 710 Margate, FL 33063 USA ("MEDIANET GROUP TECHNOLOGIES"), authorizes International Direct Response, Inc., a Pennsylvania Corporation, having an address at 1125 Lancaster Avenue, Berwyn, PA 19312("RESELLER") to be its true and lawful representative and agent for the purpose of reselling licenses of the MediaNet Group Technologies Portals ("PORTALS") and other MediaNet Group Technologies products and services in accordance with the terms and conditions contained in this Agreement.
rationale: Rule: flag market deviations or one-sided obligations. Party identification is standard; no deviation quoted.

text: RESELLER AGREEMENT
rationale: Rule: flag market deviations or one-sided obligations. Document title "RESELLER AGREEMENT" raises no concern.

text: Reseller is hereunder licensed to market MediaNet Group Technologies' Brand-A-Port portals ("PORTALS") and to resell MediaNet Group Technologies products and services for compensation in accordance with the annexed "RESELLING SCHEDULE."
rationale: Rule: flag market deviations or one-sided obligations. "licensed to market... for compensation" is a typical reseller grant.

text: MediaNet Group Technologies shall pay Reseller a fee in accordance with the annexed Fee Schedule.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided obligations. Only MediaNet pays "a fee," and the amount depends on an annexed schedule not provided.

text: RESELLER understands and agrees that MediaNet Group      Technologies is the exclusive holder of and shall retain, all right, title      and interest in and to the Portal, Content and Engine and the All Pages,      including without limitation all intellectual Property therein site      (EXCLUDING PROPRIETARY PAGES PROVIDED BY RESELLER OR BUYERS).
rationale: Rule: no IP assignment to counterparty. "exclusive holder of and shall retain, all right, title and interest" keeps IP with company.

text: The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date      and continue for a period of 1 year after the Effective Date, unless      earlier terminated as set forth herein (the "TERM").
rationale: Rule: flag market deviations. A one-year term from "Effective Date" with early termination is market standard.

text: This Agreement shall renew for successive 1-year periods, after the initial 1 Year Term, if agreed by both parties in writing within 30 days of license expiration.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. Renewal requires "agreed by both parties in writing," so it is mutual, not automatic.

text: Either party may terminate the Agreement on 60-days written notice during a renewed term.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. "Either party may terminate" on 60 days' notice is mutual and reasonable.

text: Reseller may nat assign or otherwise transfer this Agreement without MediaNet Group Technologies's prior written consent except to a successor.
rationale: Rule: assignment needs both parties' consent. Only "MediaNet... prior written consent" applies, plus "except to a successor" carve-out.

text: The laws of the State of Florida shall govern this      Agreement, without reference to conflicts of law provisions.
rationale: Rule: flag market deviations. Florida law, where MediaNet is based, is a common neutral choice.

text: Each party agrees that, during the Term of this      Agreement and for a period of five (5) years thereafter, neither will make written or oral comments regarding the other that are negative,      disparaging, tend to bring the other into disrepute or call into question the business acumen, character, honesty or integrity of the other.
rationale: Rule: flag market deviations. "five (5) years thereafter" post-term, broad mutual restriction, is longer than typical.

text: The Reseller Agreement can be terminated at any time at the discretion of either party.
rationale: Rule: 90 days notice required. "terminated at any time at the discretion of either party" sets no notice period.

text: Resellers are licensed to market the Brand-A-Port applications and receive commission on all product sales plus residual income on hosting/maintenance fees as outlined on the Compensation Schedule attached hereto.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. "as outlined on the Compensation Schedule attached hereto" relies on a schedule not provided.

text: MediaNet Group Technologies tracks the customer sales coming from the reseller and at the end of every calendar month issues a check for 20% commission to the reseller on product sales and 10% the total amount of hosting/maintenance sales made.
rationale: Rule: flag market deviations. Monthly 20% and 10% commissions on tracked sales appear broadly market-consistent.

text: Commissions are only paid each month if the amount owing exceeds $100 US.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. "only paid each month if the amount owing exceeds $100" defers payment on small balances.

text: Commission is not paid on MediaNet Group Technologies's free-ware programs.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. "Commission is not paid on... free-ware programs" excludes revenue without defining the scope.

text: BSP REWARDS PROGRAM: MediaNet shall, upon collection, remit to Member Provider _1_% of the net Rewards earned by Members through and provided directly by it, and _1_% of the net Member Rewards received and collected that is earned through Merchants, Companies, Organizations, Groups and individuals that have been contracted through Member Provider.
rationale: Rule: flag market deviations. "_1_%" placeholder rates are unfilled, leaving the reward share undetermined.

text: BRAND-A-PORT OR BSP PORTAL SALES: MediaNet shall remit to Member Provider 20% of the price of each Portal sold directly by it.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. "20% of the price of each Portal sold directly by it" limits commission to direct sales only.

text: BSP MONTHLY HOSTING FEES: In addition, MediaNet shall remit to Member Provider an amount equal to 10% of the hosting fees paid by Buyers who purchase portals or host websites with MediaNet as a direct result of the activities of Member Provider, whether those activities are sold through the portal or independent of it.
rationale: Rule: flag market deviations. "as a direct result of the activities" invites attribution disputes over hosting fee commissions.

text: MediaNet shall maintain books and records and shall provide for online confirmation of sales and payments.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. "provide for online confirmation of sales and payments" offers limited verification without full audit rights.

text: MediaNet shall permit Member Provider or its designees reasonable access during normal business hours and, upon request, to verify funds and payments due pursuant to this Agreement.
rationale: Rule: flag one-sided terms. "reasonable access during normal business hours" gives a reasonable verification right.

text: IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have caused this Agreement to be executed effective as of the day and year last set forth below.
rationale: Rule: flag market deviations. Standard execution language; "last set forth below" is a minor ambiguity in effective date.

rationale: Rule: deviation from market practice. "shall extend until the last date of expiration" of licensed rights; open-ended term.
